It sits on the organisation table beside ORGANISATIONID, which is the Data Exchange's own internal key, so the ABN is what matches a funded provider to the same entity outside the Data Exchange: to its employees in the ATO products, to its business record in BLADE, and to itself across funding rounds where the internal key changes.","dsrc":"Australian Business Register, ABN format","durl":"https://abr.business.gov.au/Help/AbnFormat","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Organisation's Australian Business Number (hashed)","k":"Australian Business Number (hashed and truncated)","def":"A hash of the Australian Business Number, truncated. The Australian Business Register defines the ABN as \"a unique 11 digit identifier issued to all entities registered in the Australian Business Register\", structured as \"a 9 digit identifier with two leading check digits\" that validate on a modulus 89 calculation. Hashing replaces it with a code carrying none of those digits, so the value cannot be decoded and is useful only for matching one record to another.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Business Register, ABN format","url":"https://abr.business.gov.au/Help/AbnFormat","lim":"The identifier stands for a registered entity, not for a service or an outlet. One entity can run many outlets and one outlet can host services from several entities, so this cannot be read as a service provider on the ground. Not-for-profit structures often place the funding agreement with a parent entity that does not deliver the service. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_organisation"]},{"n":"ACCOMMODATIONTYPECODE","d":"The kind of dwelling a client was living in, as one of twelve settings ranging from a private residence to an institutional or crisis placement.","full":"The kind of dwelling a client was living in, as one of twelve settings ranging from a private residence to an institutional or crisis placement. It is a Commonwealth Home Support Programme field, so the protocols list it among items that \"are required and will only present if the client is participating in the Commonwealth Home Support Programme activity\", and it is empty for clients of every other funded activity. HOMELESSCODE and HOUSEHOLDCOMPOSITIONCODE sit beside it on the client record and answer different questions: whether the housing is secure, and who else lives there.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.3.1 and Table 10","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The accommodation setting that best describes the living arrangement or lodging situation of a given client, represented by a label","t":"categorical","k":"DEX accommodation setting label","def":"A short label, held in the curated extract as a three-character code, drawn from the twelve settings in Table 10 of the protocols: boarding house; crisis, emergency or transition; independent living unit; Indigenous community or settlement; institutional setting such as residential aged care or hospital; private residence owned or being purchased by the client or family; private rental; public rental; public shelter; supported accommodation; other; and not stated.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.3.1 and Table 10","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The column cannot date the arrangement. The client table holds a current row plus superseded versions behind RECORDSEQNBR, so a move between settings is visible only where the provider updated the record, and there is no date attached to the setting itself. It is also not a homelessness measure, even though public shelter and crisis accommodation overlap with one: HOMELESSCODE carries that judgement, and 'not stated' is a common answer here.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"],"dom":0},{"n":"ACPR2015BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The aged care planning region the client's residential address fell in, on the boundaries used between February 2015 and April 2018. \"The Australian Government uses Aged Care Planning Regions to plan aged care services across Australia\", so this is the column that places a Data Exchange client inside an aged care supply unit rather than an ABS statistical one.","full":"The aged care planning region the client's residential address fell in, on the boundaries used between February 2015 and April 2018. \"The Australian Government uses Aged Care Planning Regions to plan aged care services across Australia\", so this is the column that places a Data Exchange client inside an aged care supply unit rather than an ABS statistical one. DSS's own address validation and geocoding service tagged it from the recorded address, in the same pass that produced the SA1 to SA4, LGA and federal electorate codes on the row.","dsrc":"Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 2015 Aged Care Planning Region maps","durl":"https://www.health.gov.au/resources/collections/2015-aged-care-planning-region-maps","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Client Address: 2015 Aged Care Planning Region Boundary Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","k":"Aged Care Planning Region, 2015 boundaries","def":"A planning region code from the 2015 determination, which the department signed in February 2015 and published as a set of whole-state region maps with a correspondence to 2011 Statistical Areas Level 2. The regions nest inside states and territories and do not cross them.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 2015 Aged Care Planning Region maps","url":"https://www.health.gov.au/resources/collections/2015-aged-care-planning-region-maps","lim":"The value is not comparable with the 2018 column beside it. The determinations were remade in April 2018 on a different SA2 base, so a client who never moved can hold two different region codes across the two columns, and a change between them is a boundary change rather than a move. The column also says nothing about aged care use: most Data Exchange clients are in programmes with no aged care component.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"ACPR2018BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The aged care planning region the client's residential address fell in, on the boundaries in force since April 2018. \"The Government signed the determinations for the current 2018 Aged Care Planning Regions in April 2018.","full":"The aged care planning region the client's residential address fell in, on the boundaries in force since April 2018. \"The Government signed the determinations for the current 2018 Aged Care Planning Regions in April 2018. These replaced the 2015 Aged Care Planning Regions.\" DSS's address validation and geocoding service tagged it from the recorded address, so it is derived geography rather than anything the client or provider entered, and it is the current-boundary companion to ACPR2015BOUNDARYCODE on the same row.","dsrc":"Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 2018 Aged Care Planning Region maps","durl":"https://www.health.gov.au/resources/collections/2018-aged-care-planning-region-maps","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Client Address: 2018 Aged Care Planning Region Boundary Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","k":"Aged Care Planning Region, 2018 boundaries","def":"A planning region code from the 2018 determination, built by aggregating whole 2016 Statistical Areas Level 2; the department publishes both the region shapefile and a correspondence from the regions to 2016 SA2s.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing, 2018 Aged Care Planning Region maps","url":"https://www.health.gov.au/resources/collections/2018-aged-care-planning-region-maps","lim":"A region is a planning unit, not a service catchment or a market. Providers deliver across region boundaries and clients travel across them, so counting clients by region measures where people live rather than where they were served. The column also cannot be compared with the 2015 column without the department's correspondence, because the two sets were determined on different SA2 vintages.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"ACTIVITYID","d":"The funded activity a service was delivered under, which the DSS metadata registry defines as \"an identifier for a unique program activity record in the Data Exchange\".","full":"The funded activity a service was delivered under, which the DSS metadata registry defines as \"an identifier for a unique program activity record in the Data Exchange\". In special_activity this is the key of the reference table itself: one row per activity, with NAME giving its title, PROGRAMID the programme it sits under, and STARTDATE and ENDDATE the window in which providers could select it when creating a case. Joining that table to the attendance, session and assessment tables is what turns a bare number on a service record into the name of the thing DSS funded.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Data Exchange: Program activity identifier, ID number'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708/","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"This data item is inclusive of all program activities with sessions recorded in the Data Exchange.","k":"DEX program activity identifier","def":"A short whole number, one to three digits in the registry's format N[NN], with no internal structure. The activity's name, its parent programme and its availability dates come from the reference table, not from the digits; SOURCESYSTEMCODE records whether the activity row came from FOFMS or an external system.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Data Exchange: Program activity identifier, ID number'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708/","lim":"An activity is not an organisation and not an outlet. The same activity is delivered by many providers from many outlets, and one provider commonly delivers several, so an activity count is a count of funding lines rather than of services on the ground. Identifiers are also not stable across programme redesigns: a restructured or renamed activity takes a new number, so a break in a series can be an administrative change rather than a change in service delivery.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_activity","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"ADDRESSSTATUSCODE","d":"Status of the outlet address presented by a code.","vp":"ai","od":"Status of the outlet address presented by a code.","k":"outlet address validation status (inferred)","def":"The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"guessed","src":"Inferred from the variable name and description","lim":"The value domain is inferred from the variable name and description, not published by the source. The values are of the right shape but are not a confirmed mapping.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"AGE","d":"A flag for whether age-appropriate development was one of the reasons a client sought assistance, defined in the protocols as \"where the client is seeking to improve age-appropriate development\".","full":"A flag for whether age-appropriate development was one of the reasons a client sought assistance, defined in the protocols as \"where the client is seeking to improve age-appropriate development\". The row it sits on is one combination of reasons, identified by ASSISTANCENEEDEDKEY, and the flags beside it cover the other domains: community, family, money, employment, education, training, material, housing, mental, personal and physical. The attendance table stores only the key, so this reference table is what unpacks that key into the set of needs recorded.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.2","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seeking assistance related to Age appropriate development","k":"reason-for-assistance domain flag","def":"A two-state flag, set when age-appropriate development is one of the reasons in the combination the key stands for. The domain names come from the eleven SCORE circumstance domains, which the protocols reuse for reasons for seeking assistance so that presenting need and measured outcome share a vocabulary.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.2","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The flag records what a provider entered as a presenting reason near the start of service, not a developmental assessment and not a diagnosis. The protocols warn that the real reason often only becomes apparent after the client engages. Reporting is optional and confined to organisations in the partnership approach, so an unset flag means 'not recorded' at least as often as it means 'not a reason'.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_assistance_needed","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"AGEATSESSION","d":"The client's age in completed years on the day the session took place.","full":"The client's age in completed years on the day the session took place. It is derived rather than reported: the protocols say date of birth \"provides a direct means of calculating the client's age\", and CONDUCTEDDATE on the same row gives the session date. Because it is recalculated for every attendance, one client's value rises across their own rows, which is what lets the attendance table carry an age profile without joining back to the client record.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.2","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Whole year age of the client at time of session","k":"age in completed years","def":"A whole number of years, not an age band. Where the client's date of birth was estimated rather than known, flagged by BIRTHDATEESTIMATED and usually set to the first day of a year, the age inherits that approximation.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.2","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"This is not the age at which a client entered a service, and it is not a person-level attribute. Because one row exists per attendance, an age distribution built straight off this column counts a person once for every session they attended, so it over-represents frequent attenders unless clients are deduplicated first.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment"]},{"n":"ANCESTRYCODE","d":"The cultural or ethnic group a client identified with, coded to the ABS cultural and ethnic groups classification.","full":"The cultural or ethnic group a client identified with, coded to the ABS cultural and ethnic groups classification. It is one of the expanded cultural and linguistic diversity items in the partnership approach, so it is optional and reported only by organisations that opted in, unlike BIRTHCOUNTRYCODE and MAINLANGUAGECODE which are part of the priority client record. The protocols specify the source list: ancestry \"records a client's ancestry if relevant. The list of values is drawn from the Australian Bureau of Statistics Australian Standard Classification of Cultural and Ethnic Groups (ASCCEG), 2016.\"","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.9","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The ancestral, cultural, and/or ethnic origin identified by a given client, represented by a code.","k":"ASCCEG 2016 cultural and ethnic group code","def":"A four-digit numeric code in the DEX curated extract, from a classification that groups cultural and ethnic groups under broad geographic-cultural groups and narrow groups. Because the field is optional partnership-approach data, a missing value carries no information about the client's background.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"ARID_HASH_TRUNC","d":"The service outlet's address, not a client's.","full":"The service outlet's address, not a client's. ADDRESSSTATUSCODE says whether the address is current.","dsrc":"ABS Address Register Information Guide","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/research/abs-address-register-information-guide","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Dex1524outlet_geocoded_addr_a1","k":"ABS Address Register identifier (hashed and truncated)","def":"A hash of the address register identifier, truncated. The ABS Address Register is the ABS's list of every known physical address in Australia, built from Geoscape's Geocoded National Address File and extended with each address's use and its dwelling structure. Hashing replaces the identifier with a code carrying none of the address, so the value has no internal structure and cannot be decoded. There is no finite list to publish.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Address Register Information Guide","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/research/abs-address-register-information-guide","lim":"The identifier stands for an address, not for a service or an organisation, so several outlets sharing a building share the value and one outlet that moves takes a new one. Truncating the hash also admits rare collisions.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"ASSESSEDBY","d":"Who made the SCORE rating on this row and whether a validated instrument was used to produce it.","full":"Who made the SCORE rating on this row and whether a validated instrument was used to produce it. The protocols pair those two facts in one field: \"the 'Assessed by' field captures whether a validated tool was used, and who made the assessment\", giving eight labels that cross SCORE directly against a validated outcomes tool, each by client, practitioner, joint or support person. It qualifies OUTCOMEDOMAINSCORE on the same row, so a rating from a client's self-assessment can be separated from a practitioner's judgement before the two are pooled.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 8.1 and Table 18","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Identifies who performed the SCORE assessment, represented by a label.","t":"categorical","k":"SCORE assessment method and assessor label","def":"One of eight labels, formed from two method values (SCORE directly, validated outcomes tool) crossed with four assessor values (client, practitioner, joint, support person). It is a data-entry date, not a service date: SESSIONCONDUCTEDDATE on the same row is when the session actually happened, and the two can be weeks apart because providers may enter data at any point in the six-month reporting period. Since 18 August 2018 it is also the field DSS uses to order a client's assessments in place of ASSESSMENTTYPE.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client_Assessment (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Created date, DDMMYYYY'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1709/","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The date and time a given client outcome assessment was entered into a system.","k":"date","def":"A date, published by the registry in DDMMYYYY form. For elapsed time between a pre and post SCORE, the session conducted dates are the fields to use.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment"]},{"n":"ASSESSMENTID","d":"The identifier of one SCORE assessment event for one client, grouping the domain ratings recorded together at a single point in service.","full":"The identifier of one SCORE assessment event for one client, grouping the domain ratings recorded together at a single point in service. ATTENDANCEID and SESSIONID on the same row tie the assessment back to the session it was recorded against, which is where the protocols say SCOREs are captured.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client_Assessment (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Data Exchange: Client outcome assessment identifier, ID number'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1709/","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"A system-generated identifier for a unique client outcome assessment record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.","k":"DEX client outcome assessment identifier","def":"A system-generated whole number of up to 19 digits, in the registry's format N[N(18)], carrying no information about the client, the domain or the date.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client_Assessment (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Data Exchange: Client outcome assessment identifier, ID number'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1709/","lim":"The identifier does not order anything. Assessments are paired into initial and subsequent SCOREs by their created dates rather than by identifier sequence, so a higher number does not mean a later assessment, and comparing two identifiers says nothing about which came first in a client's service.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment"]},{"n":"ASSESSMENTTYPE","d":"Whether the SCORE rating was taken near the start of service or later on, recorded as Pre or Post.","full":"Whether the SCORE rating was taken near the start of service or later on, recorded as Pre or Post. The protocols pair SCOREs this way: an initial rating towards the beginning of service and a subsequent rating at the end, with a further assessment every six months where practical. The DSS metadata registry warns that this field stopped being the primary ordering item on 18 August 2018 and \"should only be used to order assessments when two assessments occurring on the same day relate to the same session\", so ASSESSMENTCREATEDDATE is what orders assessments now.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client_Assessment (DEX Curated) distribution","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1709/","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The phase of service a given client outcome assessment relates to, whether the pre- or post-service phase, as represented by a label.","t":"categorical","k":"SCORE service phase label","def":"Two labels, Pre and Post, with ASSESSMENTTYPECODE holding the same distinction as PRE and POST. In long-running services a client can have several Post rows, because subsequent SCOREs are repeated at intervals rather than recorded once.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 8","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"A Post row is not an exit assessment and does not mean service ended. It also cannot be used to sequence a client's assessments after August 2018, so pairing rows on this field alone can put a later rating before an earlier one.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment"],"dom":2},{"n":"ASSESSMENTTYPECODE","d":"The coded form of the SCORE service phase, PRE or POST, matching the ASSESSMENTTYPE label on the same row.","full":"The coded form of the SCORE service phase, PRE or POST, matching the ASSESSMENTTYPE label on the same row. It marks whether the rating is the initial SCORE the protocols ask providers to record towards the beginning of service, or a subsequent one recorded at the end or at intervals to track change. Use it with ASSESSMENTCREATEDDATE, which is what actually orders a client's assessments; on its own the code only says which side of a pair a rating belongs to.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 8","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"The phase of service a given client outcome assessment relates to, whether the pre- or post-service phase, as represented by a code.","t":"categorical","k":"SCORE service phase code","def":"Two codes, PRE and POST, carrying exactly the information in ASSESSMENTTYPE. Keeping both is a convenience of the curated extract rather than two separate facts.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 8","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The code says nothing about how much time passed between the two sides of a pair, or how many subsequent ratings a client received. Because the protocols allow repeated subsequent SCOREs, a POST row is not necessarily the last word on a client's outcome and a client can have several.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment"],"dom":3},{"n":"ASSISTANCECOSTAMOUNT","d":"The dollar value of the assistance delivered in a session, for the service types that are measured by cost rather than by time or quantity.","full":"The dollar value of the assistance delivered in a session, for the service types that are measured by cost rather than by time or quantity. ASSISTANCEMINUTES beside it carries the time form, and FEECHARGEDAMOUNT is a different thing again: what the client paid, not what the service was worth.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.3.1 and Table 11","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Amount of assistance provided measured as cost, captured at the session level for the service provided. Which sessions carry it depends on the service type: DSS's program specific guidance sets, per service type, whether assistance is counted in hours and minutes, in quantity, in cost or as a type.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.3.1 and Table 11","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The amount is not the cost of delivering the service and not a payment. It is the value of assistance a provider recorded for a session under one programme's reporting rules, so it cannot be summed across programmes as expenditure, and a zero or blank means the service type is measured some other way rather than that nothing was provided.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"ASSISTANCEMINUTES","d":"The time taken to deliver a session's service, in minutes, for the service types measured by duration.","full":"The time taken to deliver a session's service, in minutes, for the service types measured by duration. It is the hours-and-minutes form of the Commonwealth Home Support Programme's amount-of-assistance item, which the protocols say is \"measured as hours and minutes, quantity, cost and/or type\", so it is populated for some service types and empty for others. Read it against ATTENDANCECOUNT on the attendance side: minutes are recorded for the session, not per attendee, so a group session's minutes are not client-minutes.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.3.1 and Table 11","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Amount of assistance provided measured as minutes (time taken to deliver a service), captured at the session level for the service provided.","k":"minutes","def":"Whole minutes of service delivery recorded against one session, with hours entered separately in the portal and carried here as a single minute total. One session's minutes cover everyone who attended, so dividing by attendance is an assumption rather than a measurement, and travel, preparation and administration around the session are outside it. Where a service type is counted by cost or quantity instead, a blank here means the wrong measure was asked for, not that no service occurred.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"ASSISTANCENEEDEDKEY","d":"A key standing for the set of secondary reasons a client sought assistance, resolved through the special_ref_assistance_needed table into one flag per reason domain.","full":"A key standing for the set of secondary reasons a client sought assistance, resolved through the special_ref_assistance_needed table into one flag per reason domain. Secondary reasons can be several at once, so the curated extract stores the combination as a key rather than as a repeating column; PRIMARYASSISTANCENEEDEDKEY on the same attendance row is the main reason. The protocols say these reasons are \"recorded at the case level, to allow organisations to reflect that clients go to different activities to address different needs\", which is why the same client can carry different combinations across activities.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.2","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A given client's secondary reasons for applying for a service, represented by a key.","k":"DEX assistance-needed combination key","def":"A whole number that indexes the reference table of reason combinations. The meaning is in the joined row: twelve flag columns covering the eleven SCORE circumstance domains, with education and skills training split across the EDUCEMPL and TRAINING columns.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.2","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The key is not a count and not a rank. Two keys cannot be compared numerically, a larger key does not mean more reasons, and nothing in the table says which secondary reason mattered most. Because reporting reasons is optional partnership-approach data, an unpopulated key means the organisation did not report rather than that the client had no secondary need.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_assistance_needed"]},{"n":"ATSICODE","d":"Whether the client identified as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, on the five-response standard the protocols take from the AIHW: no; Aboriginal; Torres Strait Islander; both; and not stated or inadequately described.","full":"Whether the client identified as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin, on the five-response standard the protocols take from the AIHW: no; Aboriginal; Torres Strait Islander; both; and not stated or inadequately described. It is part of the priority client record rather than optional partnership-approach data, so it is present for clients across all funded activities. The protocols are explicit about the last category: \"Where a client chooses not to disclose their Indigenous status, it is acceptable to record 'Not stated/Inadequately described'.\"","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.6 and Table 7","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Whether a client identifies as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin as represented by a code.","k":"Indigenous status label","def":"A short alphabetic label, two to ten characters in the registry's AA[A(8)] format, standing for one of the five AIHW Indigenous status responses. The DSS metadata registry names the element 'Client: Indigenous status, Label'.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.6 and Table 7","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"A 'no' and a 'not stated' are different answers and must not be pooled: the second is a refusal or a gap in collection, and treating it as non-Indigenous understates identification. The response is self-identified to a service provider at one point in time, so it is not a population estimate and can differ from what the same person reported to the Census or to another agency.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"ATTENDANCECOUNT","d":"The number of people the attendance row stands for, which is one for a named client and the group size for an unidentified-client row.","full":"The number of people the attendance row stands for, which is one for a named client and the group size for an unidentified-client row. DSS explains the mechanism: it adds unidentified client attendances to the attendance table and sets \"AttendanceId to the negative of SessionId, and Participation Type to 'GROUP'\", and because they are not linked to individual client records their client identifiers are coded zero. This column is what stops a large community event with no registration from looking like a single attendee.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, note on the attendance identifier","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708/","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The number of attendees who attended a given session relating to a given attendance record","k":"count of attendees","def":"A whole number of attendees for the row. The protocols cap unidentified client numbers at 999 per session and require the session figure to be no greater than the number recorded against the case.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, note on the attendance identifier","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708/","lim":"The count cannot be turned into people. Unidentified attendances carry no client record, so the same person attending three sessions of a community activity adds three to the total with nothing to link them, and summing this column across a case counts attendances rather than individuals. It also says nothing about who attended: no demographic data is recorded against an unidentified client.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance"]},{"n":"ATTENDANCEID","d":"The identifier of one person's presence at one session, and the row the assessment tables join back to.","full":"The identifier of one person's presence at one session, and the row the assessment tables join back to. DSS notes that the application \"only generates attendance IDs for individual clients\", whether they attend as a client or as a support person, and that rows for unidentified group attendance are inserted afterwards with the identifier set to the negative of the session identifier. A negative value therefore marks a group row with no client behind it, which is the single most useful thing to know before counting attendances.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Data Exchange: Attendance identifier, ID number'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708/","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A system-generated identifier for a unique attendance record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.","k":"DEX attendance identifier","def":"A whole number of up to 19 digits for individually recorded attendances, generated by the Data Exchange. For unidentified group attendances the value is the negative of SESSIONID rather than a generated identifier, and PARTICIPATIONTYPE on the same row reads GROUP.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Data Exchange: Attendance identifier, ID number'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708/","lim":"The identifier does not stand for a person or for a session. One session produces many attendance rows and one client produces many across their service, so counting distinct values counts episodes of presence. Filtering out the negative values removes group attendance entirely, which understates reach at community events; keeping them mixes rows that have no client record with rows that do.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment"]},{"n":"ATTENDANCEPROFILECODE","d":"How the clients grouped into a case relate to one another: family, couple, cohabitants, peer support group or community event.","full":"How the clients grouped into a case relate to one another: family, couple, cohabitants, peer support group or community event. The protocols say the field exists because \"data is reported to better understand the relationship between clients within a case\" and that it \"should be based on the relationships self-reported by the client and other attendees\". It is the field that separates a counselling case covering a couple from a weekly group with unrelated members, which matters because a case is otherwise just a container of sessions.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.11 and Table 17","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The relationship between clients within a case, represented by a code.","t":"categorical","k":"DEX attendance profile label","def":"One of five labels. The protocols define each: a family is two or more people, one at least 15, related by blood, marriage, adoption, step or fostering and usually resident together; a couple is two people in a marriage or marriage-like union usually residing together; cohabitants are people in residence together who are not related or in a domestic relationship; a peer support group is a planned and structured service; and a community event is a large-scale, locality-based event where attendees generally do not register.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.11 and Table 17","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The label describes the case, not any pair of people in it, so it cannot be used to build relationships between named clients. It is optional partnership-approach data and self-reported, so a blank is common and a 'family' case does not certify who is related to whom. A community event case is also where unidentified attendance concentrates, so client-level analysis of those cases will be sparse by design.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"],"dom":4},{"n":"BIRTHCOUNTRYCODE","d":"The country a client said they were born in, coded to the ABS country classification.","full":"The country a client said they were born in, coded to the ABS country classification. It is one half of the cultural and linguistic diversity pair in the priority client record, with MAINLANGUAGECODE the other half, and the protocols specify the list: \"a list of values is based on the Australian Bureau of Statistics Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), 2016\". The DSS metadata registry names the element 'Client: Country of birth, SACC 2016 code', so the vintage is fixed at 2016 regardless of when the client record was created.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.7","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The country where a given client was born, represented by a code.","t":"categorical","k":"SACC 2016 country code","def":"A four-digit numeric code. ABS describes the classification as having \"a three-level hierarchical structure that consists of major groups, minor groups and countries\", with one-digit major groups, two-digit minor groups and four-digit countries, so the leading digits give the region and the full code gives the country.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/classifications/standard-australian-classification-countries-sacc/latest-release","lim":"Country of birth is not ancestry, citizenship, language or migration status, each of which has its own column on the client record, and it says nothing about when or whether the client arrived in Australia. Because the codes are fixed to the 2016 classification, countries that have since changed name or status are coded as they stood then, which matters when joining to a later ABS vintage.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"],"dom":5},{"n":"BIRTHDATEESTIMATED","d":"A marker that the client's date of birth was worked out rather than known.","full":"A marker that the client's date of birth was worked out rather than known. The protocols allow it \"where a client does not know their date of birth or does not wish to disclose it\", and give the working example of a client who thinks they are about 30 in 2019, whose year of birth is entered as 1989 with the estimate flagged. It qualifies BIRTHMONTH, BIRTHYEAR and every age derived from them, including AGEATSESSION on the attendance rows.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.2 and Table 7","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Flag to indicate whether a given client's birth date has been estimated to the first day of a year.","k":"flag","def":"A tick box in the portal, carried in the curated extract as a two-state flag. Where it is set, the estimated date is conventionally the first day of the year, so the month has no meaning and the year is an approximation.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.2 and Table 7","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The flag does not say how far out the estimate is, and it is not a measure of data quality for the rest of the record. It also does not tell you whether the client refused or genuinely did not know, which are different situations: the first is a privacy choice, the second is common among clients without documents, and neither can be separated here.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"BIRTHMONTH","d":"The month component of the client's date of birth, kept without the day.","full":"The month component of the client's date of birth, kept without the day. The Data Exchange collects a full date of birth, which the protocols say \"forms part of the SLK and provides a direct means of calculating the client's age\", but the curated extract splits it into month and year so that a client can be aged and profiled without a full identifiable date. Where BIRTHDATEESTIMATED is set the month is an artefact of estimating to the start of a year rather than a reported fact.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.2","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The client's month of birth","k":"calendar month","def":"A month number in the registry's format M[M], so one or two digits from 1 to 12.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Client: Date of birth, Month'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709/","lim":"The column cannot give an exact age or a birthday. Combined with BIRTHYEAR it fixes age only to within a year, which is why AGEATSESSION is supplied separately, and it is not a usable component for linking to another dataset's date of birth on its own.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"BIRTHYEAR","d":"The year component of the client's date of birth, the coarser half of the split date the curated extract keeps in place of a full one.","full":"The year component of the client's date of birth, the coarser half of the split date the curated extract keeps in place of a full one. It is the column that carries most of the age information on the client record, and it is the one the protocols' estimation rule lands on: a client who believes they are about 30 in 2019 is recorded with a year of 1989 and the estimate flagged. Age at a particular service event comes from AGEATSESSION on the attendance rows rather than from this column alone.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Client: Date of birth, Year'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709/","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"The client's year of birth","k":"calendar year","def":"A four-digit year in the registry's format YYYY.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Client: Date of birth, Year'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709/","lim":"A year of birth is not an age. Two clients born in the same year differ by up to a year in age at any session, and where the estimated-date flag is set the year itself is an approximation, sometimes out by several years for clients without documents. It also cannot be combined with the month to recover a date of birth, because the day was deliberately removed.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"CARING","d":"A flag for whether a client was referred onward for help with a caring role, which the protocols define as \"support to caring role: the client is referred to help with their caring responsibilities\".","full":"A flag for whether a client was referred onward for help with a caring role, which the protocols define as \"support to caring role: the client is referred to help with their caring responsibilities\". It belongs to the referral-purpose set, keyed by REFERRALTOKEY and resolved through this reference table, and it is one of two purposes that exist here but not in the reason-for-assistance set beside it, the other being OTHER. That asymmetry is the point: a service can refer a client on for caring support without the client having come in for it.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Referred for assistance related to support for a caring role","k":"referral purpose domain flag","def":"A two-state flag, set when support to a caring role is one of the purposes in the combination the referral key stands for. The referral purposes are the eleven SCORE circumstance domains plus support to caring role and other.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The flag records that a referral was made, not that the client took it up or that a service followed. It also does not identify the client as a carer: ISCARER and HASCARER on the client record carry that, and a referral can be made for a client who has never described themselves as a carer. Referrals are session-level and optional, with one internal and one external referral allowed per session, so repeated needs appear as separate sessions rather than as a stronger signal here.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"CASECLIENTID","d":"The identifier for one client's membership of one case, so a client attached to three cases has three values and each of their attendances carries the one for the case it belongs to.","full":"The identifier for one client's membership of one case, so a client attached to three cases has three values and each of their attendances carries the one for the case it belongs to. DSS records that where an attendance row stands for unidentified group attendance rather than a named person, \"ClientId and CaseClientId are coded as 0\", which makes a zero here the marker of an anonymous attendance rather than a missing value. It sits between the case and the attendance, which is what lets a client's sessions be grouped by the case they were delivered under.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, note on the attendance identifier","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708/","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A system-generated identifier for a unique client and case in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.","k":"DEX case-client identifier","def":"A system-generated whole number, of the same shape as the other Data Exchange identifiers, with the single reserved value 0 for unidentified group attendance.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, note on the attendance identifier","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708/","lim":"The identifier is not a client and not a case. Counting distinct values counts client-case pairings, so a person who attends two funded activities is counted twice; deduplicating to people needs the client identifier, and deduplicating to services needs the case identifier. A zero must be excluded from either count rather than treated as one more client.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance"]},{"n":"CASEENDDATE","d":"The day a case stopped being open, left empty while the case is still running.","full":"The day a case stopped being open, left empty while the case is still running. A case is the container the protocols describe as holding \"one or more instances of service (known as sessions) received by a client or group of clients that is expected to lead to a distinct outcome\", and it can run across several six-month reporting periods, so this is the only column that bounds it. Read with CONDUCTEDDATE on the sessions inside the case, it gives the length of a service relationship rather than of a single visit.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 4.2","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"The date that a case ends. Null where case has not yet ended.","k":"date","def":"A date, empty where the case has not ended. It is repeated on every session row of the case in the curated extract rather than held once per case.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 4.2","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"An empty value does not mean the client is still being served. Cases are closed by providers rather than by the system, so a dormant case with no sessions for years can still look open, and a closed case says nothing about whether the client's need was met; EXITREASONCODE is the field that records why a client's relationship with the service ended.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"CASEID","d":"The identifier of the case a session or assessment belongs to, where a case is the grouping of related sessions delivered to a client or group under one activity at one outlet.","full":"The identifier of the case a session or assessment belongs to, where a case is the grouping of related sessions delivered to a client or group under one activity at one outlet. The protocols make the rules for that grouping explicit: a client attending several funded activities has a separate case for each, and the same service delivered from two outlets is two cases. The identifier is set by the provider and may be free text of up to 50 characters, but \"if left blank a system generated number is assigned\", which is why most values in the curated extract are numeric.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.2.1","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A system-generated identifier for a unique case (a number of related sessions) record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.","k":"DEX case identifier","def":"An identifier unique within the organisation, which the protocols require to exclude identifying information such as a client's name or Centrelink reference number. Portal users may leave it blank for a generated number; bulk upload and system-to-system reporters must supply one.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.2.1","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"A case is not an episode of care and not a person. It can hold a couple, a family or an unrelated group of up to 1,000 clients, so counting cases counts service containers rather than clients, and one client's continuous service can be split across several cases when they attend more than one activity or outlet. Provider-set identifiers are also only unique within an organisation, so the same value can appear against different organisations.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"CLIENTADDSOURCEVALIDCOD","d":"Address quality code","vp":"ai","od":"Address quality code","k":"client address quality grade (inferred)","def":"The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"guessed","src":"Inferred from the variable name and description","lim":"The value domain is inferred from the variable name and description, not published by the source. The values are of the right shape but are not a confirmed mapping.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"CLIENTDISABILITYID","d":"The identifier of one reported disability for one client, so a client who reported both a physical and an intellectual disability has two rows and two values.","full":"The identifier of one reported disability for one client, so a client who reported both a physical and an intellectual disability has two rows and two values. The table is a history rather than a snapshot: DSS states it \"will contain records for any disability that has ever been reported\", with CURRENTRECORD marking whether the provider still reports it. That makes this identifier the row key for a many-rows-per-client structure, unlike the one-row-per-client columns in special_client.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client_Disability (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Data Exchange: Client disability identifier, ID number'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1707/","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A system-generated identifier for a unique client disability record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.","k":"DEX client disability record identifier","def":"A system-generated whole number of up to 19 digits, in the registry's format N[N(18)], carrying no information about the client or the disability.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client_Disability (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Data Exchange: Client disability identifier, ID number'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1707/","lim":"A count of these identifiers is a count of reports, not of people or of conditions. A client can appear with several rows, some of them no longer current, and a client with no row at all has simply not had a disability recorded rather than been assessed as having none: 'None (no disability)' is a value of DISABILITYCODE, and its absence is not the same thing.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_disability"]},{"n":"CLIENTLOCALITY","d":"The suburb of the client's residential address, one of the three address parts the protocols require before a client record can be created: \"at a minimum, a client's state, suburb and postcode are considered part of the priority requirements and must be recorded to create the client record\".","full":"The suburb of the client's residential address, one of the three address parts the protocols require before a client record can be created: \"at a minimum, a client's state, suburb and postcode are considered part of the priority requirements and must be recorded to create the client record\". It is the text the provider entered, and it is what the DSS geocoder resolved into the SA1 to SA4, LGA, electorate and aged care region codes further along the row. Where a client would not give an address, the protocols direct providers to record the outlet's suburb instead, so some values describe the service rather than the client.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Client Address: Suburb","t":"character","k":"Australian suburb or locality name","def":"A locality name as entered, not a code. CLIENTADDSOURCEVALIDCOD on the same record carries the address quality assessment, which is what says whether the entered text resolved cleanly.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The suburb is not reliably the client's own. Homeless clients may be recorded at the suburb where they usually spend the night or at the service they approached, and clients at risk of family violence are deliberately recorded at the outlet's suburb, so concentrations around service locations are an artefact of that rule rather than a residential pattern. As free text it also carries spelling and abbreviation variation that the geography codes do not.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"CLIENTPOSTCODE","d":"The postcode of the client's residential address, mandatory alongside suburb and state before a client record can be created.","full":"The postcode of the client's residential address, mandatory alongside suburb and state before a client record can be created. The protocols keep the full address out of released data by converting it to statistical geography: \"a geography code is recorded in place of the client's address, which de-identifies the record\", so postcode is the coarsest address element that survives as entered. It answers a different question from the SA2 and LGA codes beside it, because postal areas cut across statistical and administrative boundaries.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.4 and Table 7","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Client Address: Postcode","k":"Australian postcode","def":"A four-digit postcode, limited to four digits in the portal and held in the registry with format NNNN. It is a postal delivery area rather than a statistical region.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.4 and Table 7","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"A postcode is not a place a client can be presumed to live in the way an SA2 can be aggregated. Postal areas are drawn for mail delivery, change without notice and include values reserved for post office boxes and large-volume recipients, so they cannot be aggregated to ABS regions without a concordance. As with the suburb, a client who withheld an address may carry the outlet's postcode.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"CLIENTSTATE","d":"The state or territory of the client's residential address, defined by DSS as \"the state or territory of an address, as represented by a code\".","full":"The state or territory of the client's residential address, defined by DSS as \"the state or territory of an address, as represented by a code\". With suburb and postcode it is the minimum address the protocols require before a client record can exist, so it is the most complete geography column on the client record and the one to use when the finer codes are missing. STE2016BOUNDARYCODE and STE2021BOUNDARYCODE beside it are the geocoder's ABS-coded equivalents, derived from the address rather than entered with it.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Address: State or territory, Code'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709/","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Client Address: State","t":"categorical","k":"Australian state or territory code","def":"A short abbreviation of up to three characters, in the registry's format XXX, rather than an ABS numeric state code.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Address: State or territory, Code'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709/","lim":"The state is the address on file, not where a service was delivered: OUTLETSTATE on the outlet record is that, and cross-border service delivery makes the two differ around Albury, Coolangatta and Canberra. As an entered abbreviation it also will not join to ABS state codes without mapping, and a client recorded at an outlet's address for safety reasons carries the outlet's state.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"],"dom":6},{"n":"COMMUNITY","d":"A flag for whether poor community participation and networks was among the reasons a client sought assistance, defined in the protocols as \"where the client is seeking to change the impact of poor community participation and networks on their independence, participation and wellbeing\".","full":"A flag for whether poor community participation and networks was among the reasons a client sought assistance, defined in the protocols as \"where the client is seeking to change the impact of poor community participation and networks on their independence, participation and wellbeing\". It is one column in the keyed set that ASSISTANCENEEDEDKEY resolves to, sitting beside family, housing, money, employment and the rest. Because the same domain names are used for SCORE circumstance ratings, a client flagged here can be followed into an outcome rating on the matching domain.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.2","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seeking assistance related to Community participation and networks","k":"reason-for-assistance domain flag","def":"A two-state flag, set when community participation and networks is one of the reasons in the combination the key stands for. The category is one of the eleven SCORE circumstance domains the protocols reuse for presenting need.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.2","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The flag is a provider's record of a presenting reason, not a measure of social isolation. It says nothing about how isolated the client was or whether the service changed that, which is what the SCORE rating on the same domain is for. Reporting is optional and limited to partnership-approach organisations, so cleared flags are dominated by non-reporting rather than by clients without the need.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_assistance_needed","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"CONDUCTEDDATE","d":"The day the session took place, which is the date every counting rule in the Data Exchange turns on.","full":"The day the session took place, which is the date every counting rule in the Data Exchange turns on. The protocols count a session against a reporting period \"if the date of the session fell within the reporting period and at least one client is attached\", and a client and a case are counted for a period on the strength of sessions falling inside it, so this column decides which six-month period a service belongs to. It is also the date AGEATSESSION is calculated against, and the service date to compare with ASSESSMENTCREATEDDATE, which is only when the record was keyed in.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 4.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The date a given session took place.","k":"date","def":"A date, published by the registry in DDMMYYYY form. Sessions can only be recorded inside an open reporting period or its 30-day close-off, so dates outside a period appear only where DSS granted a system re-opening.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Session: Conducted date, DDMMYYYY'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708/","lim":"The date does not say how long the service ran or when the client's need arose. A case spanning years is a sequence of these dates rather than a duration, and a gap between them is not evidence of a break in service, because a provider may record several contacts as one session. It is also not a measure of when the data became available: entry can happen weeks later, up to the close-off deadline.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"CREATEDDATETIME","d":"The moment the record was first written to the Data Exchange, held for every versioned table in the extract rather than for one kind of record.","full":"The moment the record was first written to the Data Exchange, held for every versioned table in the extract rather than for one kind of record. It is an administrative timestamp, not a service fact: on the activity, organisation, outlet and client tables it sits with UPDATEDDATETIME, SYSSTARTTIME, SYSENDTIME, RECORDSEQNBR and CURRENTRECORD, which together make each table a versioned history. Use it to tell when a row entered the system, never to date the thing the row describes.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client_Disability (DEX Curated) distribution","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1707/","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"The date and time that a given activity record was first created","k":"timestamp","def":"A date and time. In the DEX curated tables it accompanies the system-time columns that bound each version of a row, so the creation stamp of a superseded version and of its replacement differ.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, DEX Curated distributions","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1707/","lim":"The timestamp cannot date the event the record is about. A session recorded three weeks after it happened, an activity created long after the programme began, or a client record migrated from another system will all carry a creation time that has no relation to the underlying date, which lives in CONDUCTEDDATE, STARTDATE or the client's own fields.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_activity","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_disability","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_organisation","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_program","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_service_type"]},{"n":"CURRENTRECORD","d":"Whether the row is the version in force or one the Data Exchange has since superseded, coded 1 for current and 0 for historical.","full":"Whether the row is the version in force or one the Data Exchange has since superseded, coded 1 for current and 0 for historical. Every versioned table in the extract carries it with RECORDSEQNBR, SYSSTARTTIME and SYSENDTIME, and DSS explains how it is set: \"a service provider can delete a disability record, in which case CurrentRecord will be 0 and SysEndTime will be populated with the time that the service provider reported the disability was no longer current\". Filtering on it is the difference between the state of the world now and everything ever reported.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client_Disability (DEX Curated) distribution, note on the disability code element","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1707/","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Flag that indicates whether a record is current (1) or historical (0)","k":"record currency flag","def":"A two-state flag: 1 for the current version of a record, 0 for a superseded or deleted one, with SYSENDTIME populated when the value is 0.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client_Disability (DEX Curated) distribution, note on the disability code element","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1707/","lim":"A 0 does not mean the fact was wrong. It can mean the provider corrected an error, but equally that a circumstance changed or a record was tidied up, and the flag does not distinguish them. Filtering to current rows also does not guarantee one row per subject: DSS warns that a client may have no current disability records or several, so the flag controls currency, not cardinality.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_activity","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_disability","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_organisation","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_program","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_service_type"]},{"n":"DELIVERYORGID","d":"The organisation that actually provided the service, which DSS distinguishes from the funded body: delivery organisations are \"organisations delivering services directly to clients.","full":"The organisation that actually provided the service, which DSS distinguishes from the funded body: delivery organisations are \"organisations delivering services directly to clients. These organisations may receive funding directly or through a Funding Recipient (Lead Organisation).\" LEADORGID on the same row is the other half of that pair, so where the two differ the service was subcontracted through a consortium or delivery partnership. Join it to special_organisation for the organisation's ABN, and note that a delivery organisation may run several outlets, which OUTLETID identifies separately.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, note on the delivery organisation element","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708/","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A system-generated identifier for a unique service provider record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.","k":"DEX delivery organisation identifier","def":"A system-generated whole number identifying an organisation record in the Data Exchange. It is not an ABN: ABN_HASH_TRUNC on the organisation table carries the hashed business number for the same organisation.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution, note on the delivery organisation element","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708/","lim":"The identifier stands for an organisation as registered in the Data Exchange, not for a service or a site. One organisation can hold several identifiers where it registered separately for different programmes, and organisations that merge or re-register break a provider's history in two. Because the lead organisation is often also the delivery organisation, counting distinct values here does not count subcontracting arrangements.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"DISABILITYCODE","d":"One disability, impairment or condition a client identified with, drawn from the AIHW groupings the protocols use: intellectual or learning, psychiatric, sensory or speech, physical or diverse, none, and not stated.","full":"One disability, impairment or condition a client identified with, drawn from the AIHW groupings the protocols use: intellectual or learning, psychiatric, sensory or speech, physical or diverse, none, and not stated. Clients self-identify and \"can identify with more than one group\", which is why this sits in its own table with a row per report rather than as a column on the client record. DSS adds that the table \"will contain records for any disability that has ever been reported\", so CURRENTRECORD is what separates what a client reports now from what they once did.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.8 and Table 7","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The experience of disability, impairment or condition identified by a given client, represented by a label.","t":"categorical","k":"AIHW disability grouping label","def":"A short label held as an alphabetic code of seven to eleven characters in the registry's A(7)[AAAA] format. The protocols define each grouping by underlying condition, impairment, activity limitation and support need, giving examples: dyslexia under intellectual or learning, autism and depression under psychiatric, deafblindness under sensory or speech, and acquired brain injury under physical or diverse.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.1.8 and Table 7","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The grouping is not a diagnosis and not a severity measure. It is what a client chose to disclose to a service provider, so it undercounts conditions people do not volunteer, and it cannot be compared with a clinical or NDIS classification, which use different categories. 'None' and an absent row are also not the same: the first is a reported answer, the second is silence.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_disability"],"dom":7},{"n":"DVACARDSTATUSCODE","d":"Which Department of Veterans' Affairs card the client holds, if any, across four responses: Gold Card, White Card, Orange Card or other, and no DVA entitlement.","full":"Which Department of Veterans' Affairs card the client holds, if any, across four responses: Gold Card, White Card, Orange Card or other, and no DVA entitlement. It is a Commonwealth Home Support Programme field, listed among items that \"are required and will only present if the client is participating in the Commonwealth Home Support Programme activity\", so a blank almost always means the client is in a different funded activity rather than that they hold no card. Within that programme it is the field that flags a veteran or war widow whose care may be funded through DVA rather than through aged care.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.3.1 and Table 10","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Department of Veteran's Affairs card status, represented by a code.","t":"categorical","k":"DVA card status label","def":"One of four labels distinguishing the card types DVA issues, where a Gold Card covers treatment for all conditions, a White Card covers accepted conditions, and the Orange Card category absorbs other entitlements.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 6.3.1 and Table 10","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The card is not a service history and not proof of service. It records an entitlement status a client reported to a community care provider, so it will not match DVA's own records for people whose entitlement changed, and it says nothing about which conditions were accepted or what care DVA funded. Card status is also collected for the client, not for a partner who may be covered under the same entitlement.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"],"dom":8},{"n":"EDUCATIONLEVELCODE","d":"The highest level of education or qualification a client had completed, on a nine-level scale running from pre-primary through certificate and diploma levels to postgraduate degree, with an 'other education' catch-all.","full":"The highest level of education or qualification a client had completed, on a nine-level scale running from pre-primary through certificate and diploma levels to postgraduate degree, with an 'other education' catch-all. The protocols say the item \"lists qualifications and other educational attainments regardless of the particular field of study or the type of institution in which the study was undertaken\", so it is attainment level only, with no field of study attached.
