It is optional partnership-approach data, unlike the demographic items in the priority client record, so coverage is patchy by organisation rather than by client.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.6 and Table 16","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The highest level of education or qualification achieved by a given client, represented by a label.","t":"categorical","k":"highest educational attainment label","def":"One of nine labels, ordered by level of attainment: pre-primary, primary, secondary, certificate, advanced diploma and diploma, bachelor degree, graduate diploma and graduate certificate, postgraduate degree, and other education.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.6 and Table 16","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The scale is not the ABS level of highest educational attainment classification and does not map cleanly onto it: 'secondary education' does not distinguish Year 10 from Year 12, and 'certificate level' merges Certificate I with Certificate IV. Nor is it a currency measure, because a qualification completed overseas or decades ago is recorded the same way as a recent Australian one. EMPLOYMENTSTATUSCODE beside it records study in progress, which this column does not.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"],"dom":9},{"n":"EDUCEMPL","d":"A flag for whether education was among the reasons a client sought assistance, from the domain the protocols word as \"education and skills training: where the client is seeking to engage with education and skills training to improve their independence, participation and wellbeing\".","full":"A flag for whether education was among the reasons a client sought assistance, from the domain the protocols word as \"education and skills training: where the client is seeking to engage with education and skills training to improve their independence, participation and wellbeing\". In this reference table that single published domain is carried across two columns, with TRAINING holding the skills training side, so both should be read together before concluding a client had no education-related need. EMPLOYMENT beside it is a separate domain, despite what the abbreviated column name suggests.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.2","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seeking assistance related to education","k":"reason-for-assistance domain flag","def":"A two-state flag, set when the education and skills training domain forms part of the combination that ASSISTANCENEEDEDKEY stands for. The domains are the eleven SCORE circumstance domains the protocols reuse as reasons for seeking assistance.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols (Version 13, 1 March 2026), section 7.2","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The flag is a presenting reason recorded by the provider, not an educational assessment, and it does not identify what the client wanted to study. Because the published domain is split across this column and TRAINING, either one alone undercounts the domain. Reporting is optional partnership-approach data, so a cleared flag mostly reflects an organisation that does not report reasons.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_assistance_needed","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"EMPLOYMENT","d":"Marks that lack of paid work was one of the things a client came for, or was referred on for.","full":"Marks that lack of paid work was one of the things a client came for, or was referred on for. It is one flag among eleven on two small reference tables: on special_ref_assistance_needed a row is one combination of reasons for seeking assistance, reached from ASSISTANCENEEDEDKEY and PRIMARYASSISTANCENEEDEDKEY on the attendance record; on special_ref_referral_to a row is one combination of referral purposes, reached from REFERRALTOEXTERNALKEY and REFERRALTOINTERNALKEY. The protocols define the category as \"to change the impact of a client's lack of employment on their independence, participation and wellbeing\", and the same eleven categories drive the SCORE outcome domains, so a client's presenting reason and their rated outcome share one vocabulary.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 7.2 and 7.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seeking assistance related to employment","k":"Data Exchange outcome domain flag (Employment)","def":"A binary flag on a reference row rather than a value on a client record. A single key can set several flags at once, because a client may give more than one secondary reason and an organisation may refer for more than one purpose, so the reference table holds one row per observed combination rather than one row per category.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 7.2 and 7.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The flag says why the client presented, not whether they have a job. EMPLOYMENTSTATUSCODE on the client record is the employment measure, and the two often disagree: someone in insecure part-time work can present about employment, and an unemployed client can present about housing. Reasons are recorded at case level, so every attendance in a case repeats the same flag and counting attendances by reason counts sessions, not people.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_assistance_needed","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"EMPLOYMENTSTATUSCODE","d":"What the client said they were doing for work when the record was created or last edited.","full":"What the client said they were doing for work when the record was created or last edited. DSS defines the element as \"the employment status of a given client, whether employed or another role, represented by a label\", and the label set mixes labour force states with unpaid roles: paid work full-time, paid work part-time, unpaid work including volunteering, unemployed and looking, not working and not looking, studying full-time, studying part-time, caring, and parenting. It is optional partnership-approach data, so it is present only for organisations that opted in and for clients who were asked.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Employment status, Label' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.7","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The employment status of a given client, whether employed or another role, represented by a label.","t":"categorical","k":"Data Exchange employment status label","def":"A short uppercase label rather than a numeric code, formatted A(6)[A(10)] in the DSS registry. The protocols state the categories are \"adapted from the data collection definitions used by Disability Employment Services\", not from the ABS labour force framework.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Employment status, Label' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.7","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","lim":"One label has to carry a person who does several things at once, and the protocols say so directly: a client's employment status can also include being a carer. A working parent, a studying carer and a part-time worker looking for more hours all resolve to a single value chosen by whoever entered the record. Because the categories come from Disability Employment Services rather than the ABS, the values cannot be aligned with a Labour Force Survey or Census employment status without a mapping that DSS does not publish.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"],"dom":10},{"n":"ENDDATE","d":"When a service activity stopped being available to deliver, not when anybody stopped receiving it.","full":"When a service activity stopped being available to deliver, not when anybody stopped receiving it. Paired with STARTDATE it bounds the funding arrangement's life, so an activity ending is a program or contract closing rather than a client exiting.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/document/501","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"The date that a given activity is no longer available for service.","k":"Activity availability end date","def":"The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/document/501","lim":"The date belongs to the activity, not to any client. An empty value means the activity was still available at extract, so it is censored rather than unknown. The domain is inferred from the DIL wording.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_activity"]},{"n":"EXITREASONCODE","d":"Why the client's involvement with a case ended, recorded on the attendance row that closed it.","full":"Why the client's involvement with a case ended, recorded on the attendance row that closed it. The protocols publish nine reasons: needs met, no longer requires assistance, service unable to assist, now requires a higher level of care, moved out of area, client terminated the service, client died, no longer eligible, and none of the above. Two of them turn on cause rather than outcome, and the protocols say so: needs met is for improvement \"as a result of the reason they sought assistance and the service they received\", while no longer requires assistance covers improvement \"not necessarily because the service met their needs\".","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.16","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"This data provides information about the circumstances surrounding the ending of a client’s relationship with a case. This contributes to a general understanding of the patterns of client interaction with a program and gives indications as to reason a client might disengage with a service.","t":"categorical","k":"Data Exchange client exit reason label","def":"One of nine published labels, unordered. The distinction between the two positive reasons is an attribution judgement made by the organisation, not a measured outcome.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.16","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"Most cases carry no exit reason at all, because the field is optional partnership-approach data, so a missing value cannot be read as a case still open. The two positive categories are also not comparable across organisations: whether an improvement is credited to the service is a judgement, and an organisation with an incentive to show results has every reason to prefer needs met. Use the reason to describe how services end, not to measure whether they worked; the paired SCORE ratings are the outcome measure.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance"],"dom":11},{"n":"EXTERNREFERDETINCODE","d":"What kind of outside service a rural financial counselling client was sent on to.","full":"What kind of outside service a rural financial counselling client was sent on to. The protocols define it as an item \"used to describe a client's referral to another service from the Rural Financial Counselling Service\", and it is the only place in the Data Exchange that records a referral destination rather than a referral purpose. The twelve values are drawn from the world a farm business operates in: health professional, financial institution, legal aid or solicitor, accountant or financial adviser, real estate agent, agronomist, succession planner, social support group, training organisation, other government agency, asset agent, and other. It appears only for Rural Financial Counselling Service program activities and is empty on every other session.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 6.3.5 and the list of data values","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"This item is used to describe a client's referral to another service from the Rural Financial Counselling Service.","t":"categorical","k":"Rural Financial Counselling Service external referral destination label","def":"One of twelve published labels naming a type of destination, not a named organisation. The list is program specific and does not apply to, or align with, the general referral purpose categories used elsewhere in the Data Exchange.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 6.3.5 and the list of data values","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"A destination type is not evidence the client went. The Data Exchange records the referral as made and never records an arrival, so a count here measures counselling practice rather than client take-up. Because the field exists only for one program, it also cannot be used to compare referral behaviour between programs, and its absence on a session is not the absence of a referral: REFERRALTOEXTERNALKEY on the attendance record carries general external referrals with a purpose but no destination.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"],"dom":12},{"n":"FAMILY","d":"Marks that family functioning was one of the things a client came for, or was referred on for.","full":"Marks that family functioning was one of the things a client came for, or was referred on for. The protocols define the category as \"where the client is seeking to improve family functioning and change its impact on their independence, participation and wellbeing\", which is about how a family works rather than about who is in it. It is one flag among eleven on the reasons-for-seeking-assistance reference table and one among thirteen on the referral-purpose reference table, both reached from key columns on the attendance record.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 7.2 and 7.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seeking assistance related to Family functioning","k":"Data Exchange outcome domain flag (Family functioning)","def":"A binary flag on a reference row rather than a value on a client record. A single key can set several flags at once, so the reference table holds one row per observed combination of categories rather than one row per category.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 7.2 and 7.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"Family functioning is not family safety. PERSONAL is a separate flag on the same row and carries personal and family safety, which is where domestic and family violence work sits, so reading this column as a violence indicator both overstates it and hides the safety caseload. It also says nothing about household structure: HOUSEHOLDCOMPOSITIONCODE on the client record is the only statement of who the client lives with.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_assistance_needed","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"FED2022BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The federal electorate an address falls in on the 2022 boundaries, assigned by the DSS address validation and geocoder rather than reported by anyone.","full":"The federal electorate an address falls in on the 2022 boundaries, assigned by the DSS address validation and geocoder rather than reported by anyone. The column appears on two tables and means two different things: on special_client it is the client's residential address, and on special_outlet it is the service outlet's address, where the DIL's own label still reads 'Client Address' and is wrong. ABS defines these divisions as \"an ABS Mesh Block approximation of Australian Electoral Commission (AEC) federal electoral divisions\", so the code is a statistical rendering of the electorate, not the AEC's legal boundary.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Commonwealth Electoral Divisions","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/commonwealth-electoral-divisions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Client Address: 2022 Federal Electorate Boundary Code tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","k":"ABS Commonwealth Electoral Division code, 2022 boundaries","def":"A three-digit code: one digit for state or territory and two digits for the division, numbered alphabetically within each state. The 2022 vintage is fixed, so the code reflects the AEC boundaries in force for that year and not any later redistribution.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Commonwealth Electoral Divisions","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/commonwealth-electoral-divisions","lim":"An electorate changes under the feet of a person who never moves. The AEC redistributes divisions between elections, so this column cannot be compared with a division from another vintage, and a client appearing in a different electorate across two extracts has usually been re-coded rather than relocated. On the client table the underlying address is also unreliable for the people most likely to be studied: the protocols allow a homeless client to be recorded at the outlet's suburb and postcode, which puts them in the service's electorate.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"FEECHARGEDAMOUNT","d":"What the people attending a session were charged to be there.","full":"What the people attending a session were charged to be there. The protocols describe it as a session-level item that \"allows organisations to report whether the participants of the session were charged a fee to attend the service and reflects the program activity policy regarding fee collection\", captured as a dollar figure. It is a mandatory field only for Commonwealth Home Support Programme and Family Law Services activities, which are the two programs with a published fee policy, so it is empty across most of the Data Exchange.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 6.3.1 and 6.3.2","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The amount the participants of the session were charged as a fee to attend the service, captured at the session level","k":"Session fee in whole Australian dollars","def":"A whole-dollar number recorded once for the session, appearing in the portal only where the selected program activity and service type make it applicable. The protocols call it a number field in whole dollars only.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 6.3.1 and 6.3.2","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The amount belongs to the session, not to a client, so it cannot be turned into a price per person without assuming the fee was split evenly among everyone who attended, which for family law mediation and group sessions it usually was not. A zero and a blank also read the same way to a reader but mean different things: zero is a session recorded as free, blank is a session where the question was never asked.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"FLAG","d":"An indicator carried in from the geocoding of outlet addresses, not a property of the service.","full":"An indicator carried in from the geocoding of outlet addresses, not a property of the service. Its description in the data item list is not a description at all but the name of the source file, Dex1524outlet_geocoded_addr_a1, the same string that appears against ARID_HASH_TRUNC on the same table, so both columns came out of one address-matching run over Data Exchange outlet addresses for 2015 to 2024. On the evidence of that pairing and of the sibling columns ADDRESSSTATUSCODE, ARID_HASH_TRUNC, MB_ASGS_2021 and SA1_ASGS_2021, it marks how the outlet address resolved rather than anything a client or an organisation reported.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 4.5","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Dex1524outlet_geocoded_addr_a1","k":"Outlet address geocoding match indicator","def":"A small indicator, most likely binary, produced by the address matching process rather than reported by anyone. Neither the values nor their meanings are published.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 4.5","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"Whatever the flag marks, it describes data processing and not service delivery, so it is never an analysis variable and a difference between outlets on this column is a difference in how their addresses were written down. Because the mapping is not published, a reader cannot tell whether a set flag means a good match or a problem one, and filtering on it risks dropping exactly the outlets whose addresses were hardest to place, which the protocols say include refuges and protected locations.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"GENDERCODE","d":"The client's self-identified gender, and one of the four inputs to the linkage key that makes this dataset joinable at all.","full":"The client's self-identified gender, and one of the four inputs to the linkage key that makes this dataset joinable at all. The protocols state that \"a client's gender is recorded because it forms part of the SLK and is recorded based upon how the client self-identifies\", and that the Data Exchange uses the ABS standard with five options: man or male, woman or female, non-binary, a different term, and prefer not to answer. This is a mandatory field, unlike most of the client attributes beside it.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 6.1.3; ABS Standard for Sex, Gender, Variations of Sex Characteristics and Sexual Orientation Variables","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The identification of a client as male female and other genders which are a combination of male and female or neither male nor femaleas represented by a code.","k":"ABS Standard for Sex, Gender, Variations of Sex Characteristics and Sexual Orientation Variables gender category","def":"A short label of up to eight characters in the DSS registry, drawn from the ABS gender standard rather than from a sex classification. ABS treats gender as \"a social and cultural concept\" about identity and experience, and consolidates free-text 'different term' responses with non-binary in published output.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 6.1.3; ABS Standard for Sex, Gender, Variations of Sex Characteristics and Sexual Orientation Variables","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"Because gender feeds the statistical linkage key alongside name letters and date of birth, a client recorded as one gender at one organisation and another at a second generates two keys and appears in the data as two people. That makes the field a linkage risk as much as a demographic variable, and it makes a change of recorded gender over time indistinguishable from a data entry correction. The field is also not sex and cannot be used where a biological measure is wanted.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"GPSORGANISATIONID","d":"A second identifier for the same organisation, carried in from the grants system rather than minted by the Data Exchange.","full":"A second identifier for the same organisation, carried in from the grants system rather than minted by the Data Exchange. It sits on both special_organisation and special_outlet beside ORGANISATIONID, which is the Data Exchange's own key, so the pair is what connects a service reporting performance data to the grant agreement that funds it. The Data Exchange draws activities from DSS grants systems, which SOURCESYSTEMCODE on the activity table records, and this is the organisation half of that provenance.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026)","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Organisation GovGPS Organisation ID","k":"Grants system organisation identifier (GovGPS)","def":"An opaque identifier issued by a DSS grants management system, not by the Data Exchange. Its format is not published and the value carries no readable structure.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026)","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"Nothing in the data says what the grants system holds against this identifier, and a reader has no way to resolve it to a grant, a funding amount or an agreement period, because the grants data is not part of PLIDA. It is also not an entity identifier: two organisations under one grant, or one organisation with grants from several programs, need not have a one-to-one relationship with it. ABN_HASH_TRUNC on the organisation table remains the only key that matches a Data Exchange organisation to anything outside DSS.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_organisation","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"GPSPROGRAMID","d":"The grants system's identifier for a funded program activity, sitting on the activity table beside the Data Exchange's own ACTIVITYID and PROGRAMID.","full":"The grants system's identifier for a funded program activity, sitting on the activity table beside the Data Exchange's own ACTIVITYID and PROGRAMID. It is what ties an activity that clients attend to the funding line that pays for it, and it belongs to the same provenance chain as SOURCESYSTEMCODE on the same row, which records whether the activity came from a DSS grants system or from an external one. The activity is the level at which a program becomes something a client can attend from an outlet.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026)","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"GPS Program Activity ID","k":"Grants system program activity identifier (GovGPS)","def":"An opaque identifier issued by a DSS grants management system, not by the Data Exchange. Its format is not published and the value carries no readable structure.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026)","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The grants system is not in PLIDA, so the identifier cannot be resolved to a grant round, a funding amount or a contract term, and a change of value cannot be told apart from a re-let of the same service. It is also not a program classification: NAME and PROGRAMID on the same row carry the readable program and activity names, and this column will not group activities that a reader would consider the same program.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_activity"]},{"n":"HASCARER","d":"Whether somebody is caring for this client, which is the mirror image of ISCARER on the same row.","full":"Whether somebody is caring for this client, which is the mirror image of ISCARER on the same row. DSS defines it as \"whether a given client is the care recipient in a carer relationship, represented by a flag\", and the protocols set it as a mandatory yes-or-no question for Commonwealth Home Support Programme activities, where it exists \"to determine how many clients have care arrangements in place\". Outside that programme it is rarely populated.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Has a carer, Flag' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 6.3.1","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Whether a given client is the care recipient in a carer relationship, represented by a flag.","k":"Care recipient flag","def":"A boolean flag, held as a single digit in the DSS registry. The carer concept behind it is the protocols' own: a person providing unpaid care and support to family or friends with a disability, mental illness, chronic or terminal condition, an alcohol or other drug issue, or who are frail aged.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Has a carer, Flag' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 6.3.1","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","lim":"The carer is not a person in this data. There is no carer identifier, no carer record and no link, so a care recipient cannot be paired with their carer even when both are Data Exchange clients and both have a row on special_client. Because the question is mandatory only for one programme, a blank almost always means the client was never asked rather than that nobody cares for them.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"HOMELESSCODE","d":"Whether the client said they were homeless, at risk of homelessness, or neither.","full":"Whether the client said they were homeless, at risk of homelessness, or neither. DSS defines the element as \"the experience of unstable, inadequate or non-permanent housing identified by a given client, represented by a label\", and the protocols set the three values as Yes, No and At Risk: a person is homeless if they have no suitable accommodation alternative and their current arrangement is in an inadequate dwelling, has no tenure or only short and non-extendable tenure, or does not allow control of and access to space for social relations. At risk covers major structural problems, constant threat of violence, crowding, improvised dwellings and marginal housing such as caravan parks.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Homelessness status, Label' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.10","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The experience of unstable, inadequate or non-permanent housing identified by a given client.","t":"categorical","k":"Data Exchange homeless indicator label","def":"A short label of up to six characters in the DSS registry, holding one of three states rather than a yes-no flag. The three-part scale follows the ABS statistical definition of homelessness rather than a service eligibility test.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Homelessness status, Label' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.10","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","lim":"The value belongs to the client record, not to any session, so it is the answer as at the version of the client row you are reading. The row is versioned by SYSSTARTTIME, SYSENDTIME, RECORDSEQNBR and CURRENTRECORD, and joining the current version to an old session backdates a housing status that may have been recorded years later. The protocols also say the answer \"should be based solely on what is reported by the client\", so a service's own assessment never overrides it and a client who does not describe themselves as homeless is recorded as not homeless.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"],"dom":13},{"n":"HOUSEHOLDCOMPOSITIONCODE","d":"Who the client lives with, in one of eight categories: living alone, sole parent with dependants, couple, couple with dependants, group of related adults, group of unrelated adults, homeless or no household, and not stated.","full":"Who the client lives with, in one of eight categories: living alone, sole parent with dependants, couple, couple with dependants, group of related adults, group of unrelated adults, homeless or no household, and not stated. The protocols state the categories are \"adapted from the data collection definitions used by AIHW\" and that the classification \"is adapted to include data on whether the client is homeless\". It is optional partnership-approach data, so absence is common and is not a household type.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Household composition, Label' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.5","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Describes the client's living arrangements, represented by a label","t":"categorical","k":"Data Exchange household composition label","def":"A label of up to ten characters in the DSS registry, formatted AAAAA[XAAAA]. Seven of the eight categories describe a living arrangement; the eighth records that there is no household to describe.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Household composition, Label' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.5","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","lim":"The other members of the household are not identified. There is no household key, no link between client records and no way to find a partner or a child who is also a Data Exchange client, so this column cannot be used to build households or to attribute a service to a family. The homeless category also makes the field two variables in one: a client coded Homeless/No household has an unknown living arrangement rather than a recorded one, so dropping that category from a distribution silently drops the most disadvantaged clients.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"],"dom":14},{"n":"HOUSING","d":"Marks that housing was one of the things a client came for, or was referred on for.","full":"Marks that housing was one of the things a client came for, or was referred on for. The protocols define the category as \"where the client is seeking to improve their housing stability or address the impact of poor housing on their independence, participation and wellbeing\", so it covers insecure and unsuitable housing as well as having none. It is one flag among eleven on the reasons-for-seeking-assistance reference table and one among thirteen on the referral-purpose reference table.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 7.2 and 7.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seeking assistance related to housing","k":"Data Exchange outcome domain flag (Housing)","def":"A binary flag on a reference row rather than a value on a client record. A single key can set several flags at once, so the reference table holds one row per observed combination of categories rather than one row per category.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 7.2 and 7.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"This is a presenting reason, not a housing status. HOMELESSCODE on the client record carries the Yes, No or At Risk homelessness answer, and the two are only loosely related: a client in stable public housing can present about a repair dispute, and a homeless client often presents about money or safety instead. The Data Exchange also excludes the specialist homelessness services collection, so a DEX housing count is not a homelessness services count.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_assistance_needed","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"INCOMEAMOUNT","d":"How much the client said they earn, before tax, over whatever period INCOMEFREQUENCYCODE names.","full":"How much the client said they earn, before tax, over whatever period INCOMEFREQUENCYCODE names. The protocols state that the field is \"a numerical value for the estimated dollar amount of the client's gross income (earnings before tax)\", that it \"is based on what is reported by the client and no evidence of income is required\", and that income frequency must be recorded for an amount to be recorded at all. It is optional partnership-approach data.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.8.2","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Descibes the amount of income that a given client receives.","k":"Self-reported gross income in whole Australian dollars","def":"A whole-dollar number with no period attached to it. The web portal accepts the amount as a weekly, fortnightly, monthly or annual figure, so the number is uninterpretable on its own and has to be annualised against INCOMEFREQUENCYCODE before any two clients can be compared.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.8.2","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"This is one person's estimate of their own income, not a measured or verified amount, and it is the client's income rather than the household's, so it cannot be used to place a client against a household income threshold or a poverty line. It is also a snapshot on a client record that changes only when someone edits it, so it is not a time series and cannot show an income change over a spell of service.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"INCOMEFREQUENCYCODE","d":"The period the dollar figure in INCOMEAMOUNT refers to: weekly, fortnightly, monthly or annually.","full":"The period the dollar figure in INCOMEAMOUNT refers to: weekly, fortnightly, monthly or annually. It exists because the Data Exchange lets clients answer in whatever period they think in, and the protocols make it compulsory whenever an amount is given, stating that \"income frequency must be recorded in order to be able to record the approximate gross income\". Without it the amount beside it cannot be read.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.8.2","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Describes the frequency of income that a given client receives.","t":"categorical","k":"Data Exchange income frequency label","def":"One of four period labels. The scale is not ordinal and carries no dollar information of its own; its only job is to supply the denominator for the amount on the same row.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.8.2","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The frequency is how the client chose to quote a figure, not how often they are actually paid, so it says nothing about pay cycle, casual work or the regularity of income. A client paid weekly who answers with an annual estimate is recorded as annual. It is also no help where the amount is missing: a frequency on its own conveys nothing.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"],"dom":15},{"n":"INCOMESOURCECODE","d":"Where most of the client's money comes from, in one of six categories: nil income, employee salary or wages, self-employment from an unincorporated business, government payments, pensions and allowances, other income including superannuation and investments, and not stated.","full":"Where most of the client's money comes from, in one of six categories: nil income, employee salary or wages, self-employment from an unincorporated business, government payments, pensions and allowances, other income including superannuation and investments, and not stated. DSS defines it as \"the main source of income for a given client, represented by a label\", and the protocols state the categories are \"based on the data collection definitions used by the AIHW\". It is optional partnership-approach data reported alongside INCOMEAMOUNT and INCOMEFREQUENCYCODE.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Main source of income, Code' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.8.1","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The main source of income for a given client, represented by a code.","t":"categorical","k":"Data Exchange main source of income label","def":"A label of up to twelve characters in the DSS registry, formatted AAA[A(9)]. It names the largest single source only, not a composition, so it cannot be split or apportioned.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Main source of income, Code' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.8.1","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","lim":"A main source hides mixed income. A client on a part-rate payment topping up part-time wages appears under one heading, so the column cannot measure reliance on income support or count people with any earned income. It is also the client's own account and is not reconciled with the payments data: someone coded to government payments here may have no DOMINO record, and someone coded to wages may be receiving a payment.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"],"dom":16},{"n":"INTERPRETERPRESENT","d":"Whether an interpreter was in the room for this session.","full":"Whether an interpreter was in the room for this session. The protocols define the field as reporting \"whether an interpreter was present for the instance of service to assist with translation and facilitation\", and are explicit that it counts either kind: \"this could be an interpreter provided by the organisation or someone the client has brought along to help them\". It is optional partnership-approach data recorded as yes or no at session level, so it varies within a client's history rather than sitting on the client record.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.15","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A flag to indicate whether or not there was a language interpreter present at a given session.","k":"Interpreter present flag","def":"A yes or no flag on the session, one value per session rather than per attendee. It does not name a language and does not distinguish a professional interpreter from a family member acting as one.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.15","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"Presence is not need. A session with no interpreter may be one where the client needed one and could not get one, which is the failure most worth finding, and this column cannot separate that case from a session where none was required. Because a family member counts, a high rate of interpreter presence is not evidence of professional interpreting being funded. MAINLANGUAGECODE on the client record is the closest thing to a need measure and it disagrees with this column often.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"ISCARER","d":"Whether the client says they care for somebody, which is the mirror image of HASCARER on the same row.","full":"Whether the client says they care for somebody, which is the mirror image of HASCARER on the same row. DSS defines it as \"whether a given client is a carer in a carer relationship, represented by a flag\", and the protocols define a carer as \"a person who provides unpaid care and support to family members and friends who have a disability, mental illness, chronic condition, terminal illness, an alcohol or other drug issue or who are frail aged\". It is optional partnership-approach data recorded as yes or no.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Is a carer, Flag' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.12","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Whether a given client is a carer in a carer relationship, represented by a flag.","k":"Carer flag","def":"A boolean flag, held as a single digit in the DSS registry. The protocols state the field is \"based on the client's reported caring situation\", so it records identification rather than an assessment of caring hours or intensity.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Is a carer, Flag' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 7.12","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","lim":"Self-identification undercounts caring badly, because much of the care that meets the DSS definition is provided by people who describe themselves as a spouse, a parent or a daughter rather than a carer. The flag is also blank far more often than it is false, since it is optional, so treating a missing value as no inflates the non-carer group. Anyone counted here as a carer may separately appear with EMPLOYMENTSTATUSCODE of caring, and the two are collected under different rules.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"ISPSEUDONYM","d":"Marks a client record built on a made-up name, and so a record that will not link.","full":"Marks a client record built on a made-up name, and so a record that will not link. The protocols tell organisations that \"where a client does not wish to disclose their real name, the organisation should indicate that a pseudonym is being used and record a pseudonym that ideally is used again if the client returns for other services\". It matters far beyond privacy because the statistical linkage key is built from letters of the family and given name together with date of birth and gender, so a pseudonym changes the key.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 5.4 and 6.1.1","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Pseudonym used flag. Indicates clients who use pseudonym instead of their real name.","k":"Pseudonym used flag","def":"A tick box in the web portal, carried into the data as a flag. It records that a pseudonym was used, not what the pseudonym was and not why.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 5.4 and 6.1.1","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The flag warns that a record is unlinkable but does nothing to repair it. A pseudonymous client's key is derived from a false name, so their service history will not join to their real records elsewhere in the Data Exchange or to any linked collection, and a client who used different pseudonyms at two organisations appears as two different people with no way to detect it. Pseudonym use is concentrated in refuge and family violence services, so the linkage loss is not random and falls on the clients most likely to be of interest.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"]},{"n":"LEADORGID","d":"Which organisation holds the money for the service this record belongs to.","full":"Which organisation holds the money for the service this record belongs to. DSS describes lead organisations as \"organisations that directly receive funding from grants\" that \"may also deliver the service, or allocate the funding to other Delivery Organisations\", so the column is the funding recipient and DELIVERYORGID beside it is the provider. In a single-provider arrangement the two carry the same value; in a consortium they differ, and the difference between them is the only view the Data Exchange gives of subcontracting.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, LeadOrgId in the Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A system-generated identifier for a unique lead organisation in the Data Exchange, represented by a number (A lead org distributes funding to delivery orgs).","k":"Data Exchange lead organisation identifier","def":"A system-generated number of up to nineteen digits, following the same ID number domain as the other Data Exchange organisation and outlet keys. It is an internal key with no structure and no meaning outside the system.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, LeadOrgId in the Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708","lim":"Counting clients or sessions by lead organisation attributes a whole consortium's caseload to the head body, which for peak organisations and church-based networks can be tens of small services with nothing in common. The identifier also cannot be resolved to a named entity from the data alone: ABN_HASH_TRUNC on the organisation table is the only bridge to anything outside the Data Exchange, and it is a hash rather than a readable ABN.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ttl_priority_group"]},{"n":"LGA2016BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The council area an address falls in on the 2016 boundaries, assigned by the DSS address validation and geocoder.","full":"The council area an address falls in on the 2016 boundaries, assigned by the DSS address validation and geocoder. It appears on two tables with two meanings: on special_client it is the client's residential address and on special_outlet it is the outlet's, where the DIL's 'Client Address' label is a copy that was never corrected. ABS defines these areas as \"an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory\", and pairs on the same row with SA12016, SA22016, SA32016, SA42016 and STE2016, all cut from the same 2016 vintage.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/local-government-areas","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Client Address: 2016 Local Government Area Boundary Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","t":"categorical","k":"ABS Local Government Area code, 2016 boundaries","def":"A five-digit code: one digit for state or territory and four for the area, always ending in zero. Parts of Australia that no incorporated council administers are carried as ordinary areas named Unincorporated followed by the state or territory. Separate non-spatial special purpose codes sit outside the legally designated areas as balancing items, for people coded to migratory, offshore and shipping mesh blocks, to no usual address, and to outside Australia.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/local-government-areas","lim":"The code is a statistical approximation and not the legal council boundary, so it must never be used to decide which council an address is rated by, which by-laws apply, or who is entitled to a council service. Parts of Australia have no incorporated council at all and still carry an ordinary code rather than a missing value, so an unincorporated area enters a distribution looking like a council.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"],"dom":17},{"n":"LGA2021BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The same address placed on the 2021 council boundaries, sitting next to the 2016 code rather than replacing it.","full":"The same address placed on the 2021 council boundaries, sitting next to the 2016 code rather than replacing it. Both editions are carried on special_client and special_outlet so that a record can be matched to whichever vintage a comparison dataset uses: the 2021 code aligns with the 2021 Census and with ASGS Edition 3 geography, the 2016 code with the 2016 Census. Where the two columns disagree for one row, the address did not move; the boundary did.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/local-government-areas","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Client Address: 2021 Local Government Area Boundary Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","t":"categorical","k":"ABS Local Government Area code, 2021 boundaries","def":"A five-digit code: one digit for state or territory and four for the area, always ending in zero. There are 567 areas in the current release covering all of Australia, including unincorporated areas and nineteen non-spatial special purpose codes.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/local-government-areas","lim":"The 2021 and 2016 columns are not a before-and-after measure of anything about the client. Councils amalgamated and split between the editions and codes were reissued, so a series built by switching from one column to the other at 2021 shows a step change that is administrative. Choose one vintage for a whole analysis and match it to the vintage of whatever the geography is being joined to.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"],"dom":18},{"n":"MAINLANGUAGECODE","d":"The language the client says is mainly spoken in their home, coded to the ABS classification rather than written out.","full":"The language the client says is mainly spoken in their home, coded to the ABS classification rather than written out. DSS names the element \"Client: Main language spoken at home, ASCL 2016 code\" and defines it as \"the main language spoken at home by a given client, represented by a code\". It is one of two cultural and linguistic diversity items collected as a priority requirement, the other being country of birth, and both are recorded as reported by the client.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Main language spoken at home, ASCL 2016 code' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; ABS Australian Standard Classification of Languages, 2016","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The main language spoken at home by a given client, represented by a code.","t":"categorical","k":"ABS Australian Standard Classification of Languages 2016, language code","def":"A four-digit code from the Australian Standard Classification of Languages 2016, which covers 435 languages including 44 'not elsewhere classified' categories. The leading digit is the broad group and the first two digits the narrow group, so the code can be collapsed without a mapping table.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Main language spoken at home, ASCL 2016 code' in the Client (DEX Curated) distribution; ABS Australian Standard Classification of Languages, 2016","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","lim":"A language spoken at home is not a statement of English proficiency and not a statement of need for an interpreter. INTERPRETERPRESENT on the session record answers the second question and disagrees with this column often in both directions: a bilingual client who speaks another language at home may need no help, and a client who speaks English at home may attend with a parent who does not. The classification is fixed at the 2016 edition, which is the edition the 2021 Census also used, so the two line up; the ABS released a new edition in 2025, and language data coded on that edition will not join to this column without a correspondence.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"],"dom":19},{"n":"MATERIAL","d":"Marks that an immediate shortage of money or basic goods was one of the things a client came for, or was referred on for.","full":"Marks that an immediate shortage of money or basic goods was one of the things a client came for, or was referred on for. The protocols define the category as \"to address the client's immediate lack of money and basic items needed for day-to-day living\", which is the emergency relief end of the service system: food, bills, transport, a bed for the night. It is one flag among eleven on the reasons-for-seeking-assistance reference table and one among thirteen on the referral-purpose reference table.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 7.2 and 7.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seeking assistance related to material wellbeing and basic necessities","k":"Data Exchange outcome domain flag (Material wellbeing and basic necessities)","def":"A binary flag on a reference row rather than a value on a client record. A single key can set several flags at once, so the reference table holds one row per observed combination of categories rather than one row per category.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 7.2 and 7.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"This is the immediate-shortage category, and MONEY on the same row is the separate financial resilience category. Adding the two together double counts a client flagged for both, and treating them as interchangeable merges emergency relief with financial counselling, which are different services with different clients and different lengths of engagement.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_assistance_needed","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"MB_ASGS_2021","d":"The service outlet's address placed in an ABS mesh block, which is the finest geography on the outlet record.","full":"The service outlet's address placed in an ABS mesh block, which is the finest geography on the outlet record. ABS defines mesh blocks as \"the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS\" that \"form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard\", and the SA1, SA2, SA4 and state columns beside it on special_outlet are all aggregations of this one code. It describes where a funded service is based, never where a client lives; the client geography sits on special_client.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Main Structure: Mesh Blocks","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/mesh-blocks","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Mesh block coded to 2021 asgs","k":"ABS mesh block code, ASGS Edition 3 (2021)","def":"An eleven-digit code on the 2021 edition of the standard: one digit for state or territory and ten for the mesh block, as in 60106840000 for a Western Australian block. Mesh blocks are redefined at each Census, so a 2021 code has no counterpart in the 2016 columns on the same row.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Main Structure: Mesh Blocks","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/mesh-blocks","lim":"A mesh block is a building block, not a place. ABS releases almost nothing at this level beyond dwelling and person counts, so the code is a key for aggregating up or for computing distance, not a unit anything can be described at, and mapping outlets by mesh block produces a picture nobody can read. It is also the outlet's location, so a distance from a client's mesh block measures how far the office is, which the protocols make clear is often not where the service happened.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"MENTAL","d":"Marks that mental health and self-care were among the things a client came for, or was referred on for.","full":"Marks that mental health and self-care were among the things a client came for, or was referred on for. The DIL wording for this column, \"Whether has mental and behavioural conditions\", does not match what the Data Exchange collects: the protocols define the category as \"where the client is seeking to change the impact of mental health issues and self-care issues on their independence, participation and wellbeing\". It is one flag among eleven on the reasons-for-seeking-assistance reference table and one among thirteen on the referral-purpose reference table.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 7.2 and 7.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Whether has mental and behavioural conditions","k":"Data Exchange outcome domain flag (Mental health, wellbeing and self-care)","def":"A binary flag on a reference row rather than a value on a client record. A single key can set several flags at once, so the reference table holds one row per observed combination of categories rather than one row per category.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 7.2 and 7.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The flag is not a diagnosis and not a health condition. It records why the client sought help, so a client managing a long-standing condition well and presenting about housing has this flag clear. Where a diagnosed condition is recorded at all, it is DISABILITYCODE on special_client_disability, which carries the psychiatric grouping described in the protocols. Reading this column as a prevalence measure counts service demand instead.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_assistance_needed","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"MONEY","d":"Marks that financial resilience was one of the things a client came for, or was referred on for.","full":"Marks that financial resilience was one of the things a client came for, or was referred on for. The protocols define the category as \"where the client is seeking to improve financial resilience and change its impact to improve the client's independence, participation and wellbeing\", which is about managing money and debt rather than about how much of it there is. It is one flag among eleven on the reasons-for-seeking-assistance reference table and one among thirteen on the referral-purpose reference table.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 7.2 and 7.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seeking assistance related to financial resilience","k":"Data Exchange outcome domain flag (Financial resilience)","def":"A binary flag on a reference row rather than a value on a client record. A single key can set several flags at once, so the reference table holds one row per observed combination of categories rather than one row per category.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), sections 7.2 and 7.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The flag carries nothing about the level of income. INCOMEAMOUNT, INCOMEFREQUENCYCODE and INCOMESOURCECODE on the client record are the income measures, and a client on a high income servicing unmanageable debt sets this flag while a client on a pension who budgets does not. MATERIAL on the same row is the separate immediate-shortage category, so the two must not be added.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_assistance_needed","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"MONEYWORKSHOPCODE","d":"Which money management workshop was delivered in this session.","full":"Which money management workshop was delivered in this session. The nine are Making Money Last Until Payday, Planning For the Future, How Can Banks Help, Internet and Phone Banking, Credit Can Be a Hazard, Money Loans Sharks and Traps, A Roof Overhead - Home Ownership, A Roof Overhead Tenancy, and Managing Paperwork, with a tenth value for any other workshop. The protocols describe the field as containing \"the workshop types able to be delivered under this program activity\", allowing organisations \"to show that clients have undertaken the required training\". It only appears, and is only mandatory, for Commonwealth Financial Counselling and Financial Capability and Money Support Hubs activities when the service type Education and Skills Training is selected.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 6.3.3 and the list of data values","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Captured at the session level to indicate which of the nine workshop types clients have undertaken.","t":"categorical","k":"Money management course label (nine workshops plus other)","def":"One of ten published labels naming a specific curriculum unit. The numbering runs 1 to 9 in the published order but the workshops are not a sequence a client must work through, so the number carries no progression.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 6.3.3 and the list of data values","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"The value records what was taught in one session, not what a client completed. A client who attended a single workshop and a client who worked through all nine are distinguished only by counting their session rows, and there is no completion or attainment field anywhere in the Data Exchange. Because the field appears under a narrow condition, its absence on a financial counselling session usually means the session was casework rather than that no workshop existed.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"],"dom":20},{"n":"NAME","d":"DEX Activity Name","vp":"ai","od":"DEX Activity Name","k":"DEX program, program activity or service type name (open text)","def":"The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"guessed","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (1 March 2026)","lim":"The value domain is inferred from the variable name and description, not published by the source. The values are of the right shape but are not a confirmed mapping.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_activity","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_program","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_service_type"]},{"n":"NDISELIGIBILITYCODE","d":"What the service recorded about the client's standing with the National Disability Insurance Scheme, in one of three states: eligible, ineligible, or an access request in progress.","full":"What the service recorded about the client's standing with the National Disability Insurance Scheme, in one of three states: eligible, ineligible, or an access request in progress. The protocols say the field reports \"the NDIS eligibility of a client, and if they have an application in progress\", which is why a pending application is a value rather than a missing one. It is optional partnership-approach data and is most often populated in disability advocacy and support activities.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.13","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Describes the NDIS eligibility of a client, and if they have an application in progress, represented by a label","t":"categorical","k":"Data Exchange NDIS eligibility label","def":"One of three labels published in the protocols' list of data values. The three states are not ordered and the in-progress value is a process state rather than a degree of eligibility.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.13","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"This is the organisation's understanding, not a decision by the National Disability Insurance Agency, so an eligible label here is not an access decision and can be wrong in either direction. The NDIS data in PLIDA carries the actual access request and its outcome, and comparing the two is a check on the service's knowledge rather than a duplicate measure. Because the field is optional, blank is not ineligible.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client"],"dom":21},{"n":"ORGANISATIONACTIVITYID","d":"The funding arrangement a session or attendance sits under, holding the delivery organisation, the lead organisation and the program activity together in a single number.","full":"The funding arrangement a session or attendance sits under, holding the delivery organisation, the lead organisation and the program activity together in a single number. It exists because none of the three identifies an arrangement on its own: DSS distinguishes \"organisations delivering services directly to clients\" from \"organisations that directly receive funding from grants\", and the same provider can deliver the same activity under more than one funder. This is the level at which a grant agreement meets the data.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, LeadOrgId and DeliveryOrgId in the Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A system-generated identifier for a unique delivery organisation, lead organisation and activity pair in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.","k":"Data Exchange delivery organisation, lead organisation and activity identifier","def":"A system-generated number identifying one triple of delivery organisation, lead organisation and activity. It is an internal key with no structure, and it does not contain or reveal the three identifiers it stands for.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, LeadOrgId and DeliveryOrgId in the Attendance (DEX Curated) distribution","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1708","lim":"A change of value is not a change of provider. Because three things are folded into one key, a new lead organisation over an unchanged delivery arrangement produces a new identifier, and a provider that keeps delivering the same activity looks discontinuous. Read DELIVERYORGID for the provider, LEADORGID for the funder and ACTIVITYID for the activity, and use this column only to hold an arrangement together.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"ORGANISATIONID","d":"The Data Exchange's own key for a funded organisation, on the organisation table and on every outlet that organisation runs.","full":"The Data Exchange's own key for a funded organisation, on the organisation table and on every outlet that organisation runs. DSS defines the matching element as \"a system-generated identifier for a unique service provider record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number\". It is the join that turns a list of outlets into a provider's service network, and it sits beside ABN_HASH_TRUNC on the organisation table, which is the only key that reaches outside the Data Exchange.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Data Exchange: Service provider identifier, ID number'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1793","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A identifier for a unique organisation record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.","k":"Data Exchange organisation identifier","def":"A system-generated number of up to nineteen digits, formatted N[N(18)] in the DSS registry. It is an internal key with no structure and cannot be resolved to a name, an ABN or an address from the value itself.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Data Exchange: Service provider identifier, ID number'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1793","lim":"The identifier is a Data Exchange registration, not a legal entity. An organisation that re-registers, merges or changes its funding arrangement can hold more than one, so a count of organisations counts registrations. It also does not say whether the organisation delivered anything: DELIVERYORGID and LEADORGID on the attendance and session records carry the roles, and a registered organisation with no sessions still has a row here.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_organisation","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"OTHER","d":"Marks a referral made for a purpose the Data Exchange has no category for.","full":"Marks a referral made for a purpose the Data Exchange has no category for. It sits on special_ref_referral_to, the reference table that decodes REFERRALTOEXTERNALKEY and REFERRALTOINTERNALKEY on the attendance record into one flag per referral purpose, and the protocols define it as \"Other: the referral purpose is not captured in the list provided\". The referral table has two purposes the reasons-for-seeking-assistance table lacks, this one and CARING, because a service can send a client on for something it was never asked about.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Referred for assistance related to other matters","k":"Data Exchange referral purpose flag (Other)","def":"A binary flag on a reference row rather than a value on a client record. A single key can set several flags at once, so the reference table holds one row per observed combination of purposes rather than one row per purpose.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 7.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","lim":"A set flag tells you a referral happened and that nobody could classify it, so the column adds a count without adding information. Nothing anywhere in the Data Exchange records where the client was sent: the only destination field is EXTERNREFERDETINCODE, which exists solely for Rural Financial Counselling Service sessions. A rising share of Other means the categories are failing, not that client need changed.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"OUTCOMEDOMAIN","d":"Which part of a client's life a SCORE rating is about.","full":"Which part of a client's life a SCORE rating is about. DSS defines it as \"the specific focus of a clients wellbeing measured by a given client outcome assessment, represented by a label\", and publishes 24 permissible values that span all four SCORE families at once: circumstance domains such as HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, MENTAL and MONEY; goal domains such as SKILLS, BEHAVIOURS, KNOWLEDGE and IMPACT; satisfaction; and the community domains including COHESION. Those tokens are the same vocabulary the assistance-needed and referral reference tables use, so a client's presenting reason and their rated outcome can be compared directly.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Domain, Label'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1695","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The type of outcome domain that is relevant to the client depends on the context of the funded activity being delivered. Organisations should only report a numerical rating against the domain(s) that are most relevant for their client and the outcomes they are aiming to achieve.","t":"categorical","k":"Data Exchange SCORE outcome domain label","def":"A label of up to seventeen characters, formatted AAA[A(14)], with 24 permissible values plus a supplementary UNKNOWN.
