The label must be read with OUTCOMETYPE, which says which SCORE family the domain belongs to.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Domain, Label'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1695","lim":"The set of domains present describes what the service was required or chose to rate, not what mattered to the client. The protocols set a floor and leave the rest to the organisation: providers are \"at a minimum, required to report SCOREs for Circumstance domains listed in the Program Specific Guidance\", and should \"otherwise report a rating against the domain(s) that are most relevant for their client and the outcomes they are aiming to achieve\". A domain that is absent was therefore never assessed and cannot be read as a domain in which the client was doing fine, and comparing the domain mix between two organisations compares their programs and their guidance.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment"],"dom":22},{"n":"OUTCOMEDOMAINSCORE","d":"The rating itself, from 1 to 5, for the domain named on the same row.","full":"The rating itself, from 1 to 5, for the domain named on the same row. The protocols anchor both ends: 1 means the client's circumstances are \"having a significant negative impact on their independence, participation and wellbeing\", and 5 means they are \"adequate and stable over the medium term\" to support it, with 3 as a middle ground between the two negative ratings and the two adequate ones. The scale is the same for all four SCORE families, which is what lets circumstances, goals, satisfaction and community outcomes be reported together.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Domain rating, Five-point scale'; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 8.2.2","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1922","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"An outcome domain rating recorded for a given client outcome assessment, represented by a score 1-5.","t":"categorical","k":"Data Exchange SCORE five-point rating","def":"A single digit, 1 to 5, ordinal and with the same direction in every domain: higher is better. The five points are defined by impact on independence, participation and wellbeing rather than by any underlying measurement unit.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Domain rating, Five-point scale'; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 8.2.2","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1922","lim":"A level is not comparable between clients or between organisations. ASSESSEDBY on the same row records who made the judgement, and the protocols allow the client, the practitioner, both jointly or a support person, using either the SCORE scale directly or a validated instrument translated onto it, so a one-point gap between two rows can be a difference in assessor or in tool. The design use is the change within one client between a paired initial and follow-up rating, not the level.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment"],"dom":23},{"n":"OUTCOMEDOMAINSCORECODE","d":"The domain and the rating fused into one token, such as HOUSING3 or MONEY4.","full":"The domain and the rating fused into one token, such as HOUSING3 or MONEY4. DSS defines it as \"an outcome domain rating recorded for a given client outcome assessment, represented by a label\" and publishes 60 permissible values of the form domain name followed by a digit. It is worth reaching for over the two columns beside it because each value carries the wording the protocols give that rating in that specific domain, rather than the generic scale, and DSS records that \"the permissible values and their meaning are taken from the Data Exchange Protocols\".","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Domain rating, Label'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1923","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"An outcome domain rating recorded for a given client outcome assessment, represented by a code.","k":"Data Exchange SCORE domain and rating label","def":"A string of up to eighteen characters, formatted AAA[A(14)]N: a domain label with a trailing digit from 1 to 5. There are 60 values, covering twelve domains at five ratings each.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Domain rating, Label'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1923","lim":"It is a string and will not sort, average or difference. Reading it as an ordinal means splitting off the trailing digit, at which point OUTCOMEDOMAINSCORE already holds the number. The 60 values also cover fewer domains than the 24 labels OUTCOMEDOMAIN admits, so this column and the domain column are not interchangeable and a filter written against one will not select the same rows as the same filter written against the other.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment"]},{"n":"OUTCOMETYPE","d":"Which of the four SCORE families a rating belongs to: circumstances, goals, satisfaction or group and community.","full":"Which of the four SCORE families a rating belongs to: circumstances, goals, satisfaction or group and community. DSS defines it as \"the focus of a clients wellbeing measured by a given client outcome assessment, represented by a label\" and publishes exactly those four values. The column appears on both special_client_assessment and special_community_assessment, and the split is clean: the first three occur on the client table and the group value on the community table, because a community SCORE rates a group's capacity rather than a person's circumstances.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Domain group, Label'","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1687","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The type of outcomes measured through SCORE (for client assessment outcome types are Satisfaction, Goals, Circumstances)","t":"categorical","k":"Data Exchange SCORE domain group label","def":"A label of up to thirteen characters, formatted AAAAA[A(8)], taking one of four values. It groups the domains in OUTCOMEDOMAIN rather than adding information of its own, which is why a domain label is ambiguous without it.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Domain group, Label'","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1687","lim":"The type says which family a rating is in, not where it sits in a client's service. Whether a rating is an initial or a follow-up SCORE is carried by ASSESSMENTTYPE, and DSS notes that since 18 August 2018 even that field \"is no longer the primary item used to determine assessment order\" and should only order assessments made on the same day for the same session. Pairing an initial and follow-up rating therefore needs the assessment dates, not this column.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment"],"dom":24},{"n":"OUTLETACTIVITYID","d":"Which funded activity, at which outlet, this session belongs to.","full":"Which funded activity, at which outlet, this session belongs to. The pair exists because the two do not determine each other: the protocols state that \"the organisation identifies the program activities each outlet delivers\", so one outlet can run several activities and one activity can run from many outlets. That makes this the delivery unit on the ground, and the level at which a question like how many sessions this service ran from this office is actually answerable.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols, version 13 (effective 1 March 2026), section 4.5","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2026-02/3016-dex-protocols-update-march.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A system-generated identifier for a unique outlet and activity pair in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.","k":"Data Exchange outlet and activity pair identifier","def":"A system-generated number, unique to one combination of outlet and program activity. ORGANISATIONACTIVITYID on the same session row carries the delivery organisation, lead organisation and activity together, and DELIVERYORGID carries the provider, so an outlet operating under a consortium cannot be attributed to a funder from this column alone. The pair is also a configuration record: it exists once an organisation registers an outlet to deliver an activity, whether or not any client was ever seen there.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"OUTLETID","d":"Which service location a record belongs to, appearing on the outlet table itself and on every table that needs to place a service: attendance, session, client assessment and community assessment.","full":"Which service location a record belongs to, appearing on the outlet table itself and on every table that needs to place a service: attendance, session, client assessment and community assessment. DSS defines it as \"a system-generated identifier for a unique outlet record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number\", and the protocols define an outlet as \"the physical location from where a service is primarily being delivered\". It joins to special_outlet, where the outlet's suburb, postcode, state and geocoded boundaries sit.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Data Exchange: Outlet identifier, ID number'; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 4.5","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/274","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A identifier for a unique outlet record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.","k":"Data Exchange outlet identifier","def":"A system-generated number of up to nineteen digits, formatted N[N(18)] in the DSS registry. It is an internal key with no structure and no meaning outside the Data Exchange.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Data Exchange: Outlet identifier, ID number'; DSS Data Exchange Protocols version 13, section 4.5","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/274","lim":"An outlet is where staff are based, not where the client was seen. The protocols direct organisations to use the nearest administrative premises for mobile services, to use a nearby public place such as a post office or shopping centre for a refuge, and never to create an outlet at a client's home. Distance between an outlet and a client's address is therefore a distance to an office, not to a service. SERVICESETTINGCODE on the session record is what says whether the service happened at the outlet at all.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"OUTLETLOCALITY","d":"The suburb of the service outlet, as the funded organisation registered it in the Data Exchange.","full":"The suburb of the service outlet, as the funded organisation registered it in the Data Exchange. The protocols define an outlet as \"the physical location from where a service is primarily being delivered\", so this is where staff are based rather than where a client was seen. It sits with OUTLETPOSTCODE and OUTLETSTATE as the address the organisation typed in, and with ARID_HASH_TRUNC and the ASGS columns as that same address geocoded, which makes it the plain-language label for a row whose other location columns are all codes.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 3.5","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Outlet Address: Suburb","t":"character","k":"Australian locality (suburb) name","def":"Free text holding an Australian locality or suburb name as the organisation entered it, not a code drawn from a classification. There is no validation list behind the field, so spelling, case, abbreviation and the treatment of multi-word names vary between organisations and over time.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 3.5","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"The suburb belongs to the outlet, not to the service delivery. The protocols direct organisations running mobile services to register the nearest administrative premises staff travel from, and to replace a refuge or other protected address with a nearby public place such as a post office or shopping centre, so tallying activity by outlet suburb overstates the suburbs where staff sit and understates the ones where people are helped.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"OUTLETPOSTCODE","d":"The postcode of the premises a funded service is delivered from, one of the three parts of the outlet address the organisation keyed into the Data Exchange.","full":"The postcode of the premises a funded service is delivered from, one of the three parts of the outlet address the organisation keyed into the Data Exchange. It is the column that supports the comparison the protocols describe between where clients live and where services sit, set against CLIENTPOSTCODE on special_client. Because the value belongs to the outlet's registration, it changes only when the organisation edits the outlet record, not when a service moves.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, value domain 'Australian postcode code', Aristotle item 78","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/78","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Outlet Address: Postcode","k":"Australian postcode","def":"A four-digit Australian postcode. DSS registers the domain as \"the Postcode datafile code set representing Australian postcodes as defined by Australia Post\", with 0097 reserved for not applicable, 0098 for unknown and 0099 as the default, so the field is a four-character string and leading zeros are meaningful.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, value domain 'Australian postcode code', Aristotle item 78","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/78","lim":"A postcode is a mail delivery area, not a statistical one: postcodes do not nest inside SA2s or local government areas, several can cover one suburb name, and some cover only post office boxes. Anything that has to line up with ABS geography should use the SA and mesh block columns on the same row rather than this field.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"OUTLETSTATE","d":"The jurisdiction the service outlet sits in, and the coarsest of the three address fields the organisation registered for it.","full":"The jurisdiction the service outlet sits in, and the coarsest of the three address fields the organisation registered for it. DSS commissions many Data Exchange activities state by state and reports against them the same way, so this is the column that splits a national provider's outlets by administering jurisdiction. STATE_ASGS_2021 on the same row is the same fact derived by ABS from the geocoded address, and is the one to use when the analysis has to join to ABS geography.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, value domain 'Australian State or Territory Code', Aristotle item 81","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/81","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Outlet Address: State","t":"categorical","k":"Australian state or territory","def":"A state or territory as recorded on the address. DSS registers its state domain as a three-character abbreviation set covering ACT, NSW, NT, QLD, SA, TAS, VIC and WA, with EXT for the other territories and IOB for International Operations Branch, so expect character values rather than the one-digit ABS code carried by the STE boundary columns beside it.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, value domain 'Australian State or Territory Code', Aristotle item 81","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/81","lim":"This is the jurisdiction of the premises, not of the client and not of the funder. A border outlet serves clients from the neighbouring state, and a national program delivered from a single head office reports every one of its sessions against that one state. For a client's own jurisdiction, CLIENTSTATE on special_client is the field.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"],"dom":6},{"n":"PARTICIPATIONTYPE","d":"Whether the person was at the session as a client or as someone accompanying one.","full":"Whether the person was at the session as a client or as someone accompanying one. DSS draws the line this way: \"A client is a primary recipient of service, and a support person is an individual who is attending the session in order to provide some form of support to the client or clients, but is not receiving that service themselves.\" Which cohort counts as the client is decided activity by activity, so in Family Law Services the children are the clients and the parents in the room are support persons. On special_client_assessment the same column says whose outcome a SCORE rating belongs to.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client: Participation type, Label', Aristotle item 296","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/296","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"The role of a given client at a session, represented by a label.","t":"categorical","k":"DEX participation type label","def":"A short uppercase label. Recording support persons is optional, so their absence is no evidence that a client attended alone, and GROUP rows carry no client identifier at all, which means filtering to CLIENT silently discards the aggregate attendance of large groups.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment"],"dom":25},{"n":"PERSONAL","d":"A flag marking that personal and family safety is one of the domains carried by the key this reference row decodes.","full":"A flag marking that personal and family safety is one of the domains carried by the key this reference row decodes. The protocols define the domain as \"Personal and family safety: where the client is seeking to change the impact of personal and family safety issues on their independence, participation and wellbeing\". On special_ref_assistance_needed the column expands a reason-for-assistance key; on special_ref_referral_to it expands a referral purpose key, so the same flag answers two different questions depending on which table it is read from. It is only meaningful after joining the key back to the attendance rows that point at it.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, sections 6.2 and 6.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seeking assistance related to Personal and family safety","k":"Personal and family safety outcome domain flag","def":"One flag column in a wide decode of a reasons key. Its siblings are the other standard domains, AGE, COMMUNITY, EDUCEMPL, EMPLOYMENT, FAMILY, HOUSING, MATERIAL, MENTAL, MONEY, PHYSICAL and TRAINING, with CARING and OTHER added in the referral table, and one key can set several of them at once.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, sections 6.2 and 6.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"A set flag records the domain a practitioner chose near the start of service, which the protocols warn is often not the client's real need: they note the real reason is frequently not apparent until after the client engages. It appears twice in the product with different meanings: on special_ref_assistance_needed it is a reason the client came, and on special_ref_referral_to it is a purpose the client was sent on for.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, sections 6.2 and 6.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seeking assistance related to Physical health","k":"Physical health outcome domain flag","def":"A flag in the wide decode of a reasons key, one of the eleven standardised domains that also form the SCORE circumstance domains. ASSISTANCENEEDEDKEY sits beside it on the same attendance row and holds the secondary reasons, which the protocols expect to be one or two more.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.2","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A given client's main reason for applying for a service, represented by a key.","k":"DEX reason-for-assistance key (primary)","def":"An integer key into the special_ref_assistance_needed reference table rather than a code that can be read on its own. The values are of the right shape but are not a confirmed mapping.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ttl_priority_group"],"dom":26},{"n":"PROGRAMID","d":"The funding program a program activity belongs to, defined by DSS as \"an identifier for a unique program record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number\".","full":"The funding program a program activity belongs to, defined by DSS as \"an identifier for a unique program record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number\". On special_program it is the key of the program lookup, paired with NAME; on special_activity it says which program each activity rolls up to, which makes it the column that reduces a long list of activities to the handful of budget programs reported against. The published values run from 20, Programme 2.1 Families and Communities, to 30, Program 2.4 Refugee and Humanitarian Assistance, and include state agencies such as the NSW Department of Communities and Justice as well as NDIA and aged care lines.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Data Exchange: Program identifier, ID number', Aristotle item 1396","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1396","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The name by which a defined package of services or activities usually sponsored or administered by local state or national governments or by another authoritative entity that aims to accomplish a specified end or objective is identified as represented by a code.","k":"DEX program identifier","def":"A two-digit number from a short published list. Each value carries a start date, the earliest being 4 September 2015, and one value has closed: 24, NSW Family and Community Services, ended on 1 August 2019 and was replaced by 25, NSW Department of Communities and Justice.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Data Exchange: Program identifier, ID number', Aristotle item 1396","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1396","lim":"The program is a funding line, not a service. Two activities under one program can be quite different kinds of help, and a client counted under a program has not necessarily received anything its title suggests. Because programs are renamed and renumbered when agencies restructure, a series that spans one of those changes will break unless the old and new values are combined by hand.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_activity","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_program"]},{"n":"RECORDSEQNBR","d":"The position of this row in the version history of the record it describes.","full":"The position of this row in the version history of the record it describes. The seven reference tables that carry it — activity, client, client disability, organisation, outlet, program and service type — are delivered as full histories rather than snapshots, so one outlet or one client appears once per version and this column orders those versions. CURRENTRECORD flags which version is live and SYSSTARTTIME and SYSENDTIME give the window each was in force; count without filtering on one of them and a single outlet becomes several.","dsrc":"Inferred from the variable name, its table and the custodian's own wording","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Record sequence number (sequence of historical records)","k":"record version sequence number","def":"A positive integer counting upwards within one entity's history, so it is unique only in combination with that entity's identifier and is never a key on its own.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client (DEX Curated) distribution, which lists the column beside CurrentRecord, SysStartTime and SysEndTime without publishing its definition","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/policy","lim":"A new sequence number means a field on the record changed, not that anything happened to the client or the service: a corrected postcode and a genuine relocation both produce one. The protocols put it plainly: \"Referral source is the person or agency responsible for referring a client to an organisation.\" The categories follow AIHW collection definitions and fall into agency sources such as health, community services, education, legal, employment, Centrelink, My Aged Care, NDIS and Local Area Coordinator referrals, non-agency sources such as self, family, friends and a general practitioner, and a not stated category. It answers how people reach a service, which the outward referral columns on the same row cannot.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.3","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Referral source is the person or agency responsible for referring a client to an organisation.","t":"categorical","k":"DEX referral source category","def":"A label from a fixed list of about twenty categories grouped under agency, non-agency and not stated. The agency group is the long one, running from health, community services, educational and legal agencies through to 'Lender/financial agency', 'Accounting agency', Centrelink, My Aged Care Gateway and the NDIS and Local Area Coordinator referral categories.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.3","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"The source is recorded once per case, so a client who returns through a different pathway keeps the value from the first time, and a case that ran for years still shows how it began. 'Self' also covers two different things, a genuine self-referral and a client who could not say who suggested the service, and the field is optional, so blank means unrecorded far more often than unknown.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance"],"dom":27},{"n":"REFERRALTOEXTERNALDATE","d":"The date a referral out to a different organisation was recorded against this session.","full":"The date a referral out to a different organisation was recorded against this session. It pairs with REFERRALTOEXTERNALKEY, which says what the referral was for, and mirrors REFERRALTOINTERNALDATE for referrals kept inside the same provider. Because the protocols allow only one external referral per session record, a client sent to two outside services on one day has to appear as two sessions, so this date can be repeated across sessions that describe a single conversation.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Date referral to other service (external) was made","k":"date","def":"A calendar date at day resolution. Data Exchange dates are entered as dd/mm/yyyy and the registry's session dates are registered in DDMMYYYY form, so there is no time component to work with.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"It records that a referral was made, not that the client ever arrived: nothing in the Data Exchange links this row to a later record at the receiving organisation, so referral counts cannot be turned into service take-up. Since the referral is captured on the session record, the date normally sits on the session itself and is not an independent event date.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance"]},{"n":"REFERRALTOEXTERNALKEY","d":"The key describing why a client was referred out of this organisation at this session.","full":"The key describing why a client was referred out of this organisation at this session. The protocols define the external type as a referral \"made to a service that is provided by a different organisation\", as against the internal type carried by REFERRALTOINTERNALKEY. Join the value to special_ref_referral_to to expand it into the thirteen referral purpose flags, which are the eleven SCORE outcome domains plus support to a caring role and other.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Referrals made to other services to reflect a client’s need for help outside the scope of the funded activity - referral made to a service that is provided by a different organisation","k":"DEX referral purpose key (external referral)","def":"An integer key into the special_ref_referral_to lookup rather than a purpose code in its own right. The row it points at can set more than one purpose flag, so one key can carry several reasons for the referral.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"One external referral is permitted per session, so the column undercounts a session in which several outside referrals were made unless the organisation split them across sessions. It names a purpose and never a destination, so it cannot be used to map which agencies receive referrals or to check whether the receiving service exists.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance"]},{"n":"REFERRALTOINTERNALDATE","d":"The date a client was referred to another service inside the same organisation at this session.","full":"The date a client was referred to another service inside the same organisation at this session. With REFERRALTOINTERNALKEY it forms half of the client pathways data the protocols place at session level, the other half being the external referral columns on the same row. Both are extended partnership-approach items, so the column is populated only for organisations that agreed to collect the extended data set.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Date referral to other service (internal) was made","k":"date","def":"A calendar date at day resolution, entered as dd/mm/yyyy in the Data Exchange, with no time component.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"An internal referral moves a client between services within one provider, so it produces no new organisation anywhere in the data and cannot be traced to an outcome. A provider that runs a single funded activity has nowhere to refer internally, so a low rate of internal referral dates reflects how many services a provider operates as much as how often it refers.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance"]},{"n":"REFERRALTOINTERNALKEY","d":"The key describing why a client was moved to another service within the same organisation at this session.","full":"The key describing why a client was moved to another service within the same organisation at this session. The protocols define this type as a referral \"made to another service offered within the same organisation\", which is the whole difference between this column and REFERRALTOEXTERNALKEY. Both resolve through the same lookup, special_ref_referral_to, so the purpose vocabulary is shared and only the direction differs.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Referrals made to other services to reflect a client’s need for help outside the scope of the funded activity - referral made to another service offered within the same organisation","k":"DEX referral purpose key (internal referral)","def":"An integer key into the special_ref_referral_to lookup. The row it resolves to sets one or more of the thirteen referral purpose flags, so a single key value can stand for several purposes at once.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"It cannot tell you which internal service received the client, only what the referral was for, and there is no link to the case or session the client turned up in next. Because both key columns point at the same lookup, reading the purpose without also checking which column it came from loses the internal against external distinction that is the point of the pair.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance"]},{"n":"REFERRALTOKEY","d":"The primary key of the referral purpose lookup: each row is one combination of purposes, with the flags AGE, CARING, COMMUNITY, EDUCEMPL, EMPLOYMENT, FAMILY, HOUSING, MATERIAL, MENTAL, MONEY, OTHER, PERSONAL, PHYSICAL and TRAINING beside it.","full":"The primary key of the referral purpose lookup: each row is one combination of purposes, with the flags AGE, CARING, COMMUNITY, EDUCEMPL, EMPLOYMENT, FAMILY, HOUSING, MATERIAL, MENTAL, MONEY, OTHER, PERSONAL, PHYSICAL and TRAINING beside it. REFERRALTOINTERNALKEY and REFERRALTOEXTERNALKEY on special_attendance both point here. The purposes are the SCORE outcome domains extended with support to a caring role and a residual category the protocols describe as \"Other: the referral purpose is not captured in the list provided\".","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The key to record why a client was referred onward for assistance","k":"DEX referral purpose key","def":"An integer key on a decode table, so the table holds one row per distinct combination of purposes rather than one row per client, referral or session, and it carries no dates or identifiers of its own.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 6.4","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"The table tells you which combinations of purposes exist, never how often any of them occur; those counts have to come from the attendance rows that reference it. Because one key table serves both the internal and the external referral columns, a key on its own does not say what kind of referral produced it.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"REPORTINGPERIODENDTIME","d":"The closing timestamp of the six-month Data Exchange reporting period that a calendar date falls in. special_ref_calendar is a date dimension with one row per date, and this column is the boundary that decides which period a session dated on that day is counted in, with THEREPORTINGPERIOD naming the same period.","full":"The closing timestamp of the six-month Data Exchange reporting period that a calendar date falls in. special_ref_calendar is a date dimension with one row per date, and this column is the boundary that decides which period a session dated on that day is counted in, with THEREPORTINGPERIOD naming the same period. The protocols set two standardised six-monthly performance reporting periods each year, so joining a session date to this table is how period labels are kept consistent across activities.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 10.3","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"DEX reporting period end timestamp","def":"A timestamp marking the end of a reporting period, repeated on every calendar row inside that period. Because periods run in half-years, the column takes only two distinct values a year across a very large number of rows.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, section 10.3","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"It bounds the period, not the data. Organisations have a further 30-day close-off window after a period ends in which they can still amend what they reported, and data outside a closed period can be entered later if a system re-open is granted, so this timestamp says nothing about when the records for that period became complete.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"SA1_ASGS_2021","d":"The SA1 the service outlet's address falls in, coded by ABS from the address matched behind ARID_HASH_TRUNC rather than by the DSS geocoder.","full":"The SA1 the service outlet's address falls in, coded by ABS from the address matched behind ARID_HASH_TRUNC rather than by the DSS geocoder. ABS defines SA1s as \"geographic areas built from whole Mesh Blocks\" that are \"designed to maximise the geographic detail available for Census of Population and Housing data\". It belongs to the ABS block on special_outlet alongside MB_ASGS_2021, SA2_ASGS_2021, SA4_ASGS_2021 and STATE_ASGS_2021, which is the set to use when outlet location has to line up with Census, SEIFA or other PLIDA geography rather than with the DSS boundary codes on the same row.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-1","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Sa1 location","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 1 code","def":"An 11-digit fully hierarchical code under ASGS Edition 3, July 2021 to June 2026: one digit for state or territory, two for SA4, two for SA3, four for SA2 and two for SA1, as in 50302104118. There are 61,845 SA1s, including 34 non-spatial special purpose codes for populations such as people in transit or with no fixed address. The older 7-digit short code is not used in Edition 3.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-1","lim":"The code locates premises, not people. An SA1 holds 200 to 800 residents, but an outlet's SA1 says nothing about where its clients live, and a CBD office block puts many providers in one SA1 while each serves a whole region. It is also not comparable with the client SA1 columns on special_client, which come from the DSS geocoder rather than from the ABS address match.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"SA12016BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The 2016-vintage SA1 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address on the record: the client's residential address on special_client, the outlet's premises on special_outlet.","full":"The 2016-vintage SA1 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address on the record: the client's residential address on special_client, the outlet's premises on special_outlet. DSS registers the element as \"the code that represents a designated region representing the smallest unit for the release of Census data used for describing a location\", stored as an 11-character value. The custodian's own note that it was \"tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)\" is what separates this column from ABS's SA1_ASGS_2021 on the outlet table, which is derived from the address register match instead.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Address: Statistical Area, Level 1 (SA1) Code (ASGS 2016) N(11)', Aristotle item 72709","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Client Address: SA1 2016 Boundary Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 1 code","def":"An 11-digit code on the ASGS July 2016 edition, hierarchical from state through SA4, SA3 and SA2 down to the SA1. The Data Exchange carries 2011, 2016 and 2021 SA1 columns side by side because the boundaries are redrawn for each Census edition.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Address: Statistical Area, Level 1 (SA1) Code (ASGS 2016) N(11)', Aristotle item 72709","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/72709","lim":"The vintages are not interchangeable. Boundaries move between ASGS editions, so the 2016 and 2021 codes on one row are not two names for the same area and a time series has to be built on one vintage or concorded between them. For a client, the address behind the code is the one held on the client record, which the protocols allow to be the outlet's suburb where the client is homeless or fears for their safety.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"SA12021BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The 2021-vintage SA1 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address on the record, on the client's residence in special_client and on the outlet's premises in special_outlet.","full":"The 2021-vintage SA1 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address on the record, on the client's residence in special_client and on the outlet's premises in special_outlet. It was added with the rest of the 2021 boundary family when the Data Exchange re-coded stored addresses to ASGS Edition 3, which is why the DSS registry still lists the 2011 and 2016 columns beside it. This is the finest DSS-coded geography in the product and the one that joins to 2021 Census output and to SEIFA 2021.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-1","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Client Address: SA1 2021 Boundary Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 1 code","def":"An 11-digit code under ASGS Edition 3, July 2021 to June 2026, hierarchical from state through SA4, SA3 and SA2. There are 61,845 SA1s, of which 34 are non-spatial special purpose codes covering people in transit or with no fixed address.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-1","lim":"Re-coding is applied to the address as it stands in the record, so an old client row can carry a current 2021 code for an address the client left years ago: the geography is fresh, the residence is not. On special_outlet it is also not the same column as SA1_ASGS_2021, which ABS derived through the address register, so the two can place one outlet in different SA1s.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"SA2_ASGS_2021","d":"The SA2 containing the service outlet's address, coded by ABS from the address register match rather than by the DSS geocoder.","full":"The SA2 containing the service outlet's address, coded by ABS from the address register match rather than by the DSS geocoder. ABS defines SA2s as \"medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s)\" whose \"purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically\". Most ABS statistics that are not from the Census are published at this level, so it is the practical unit for setting outlet locations against population, income or health estimates.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Sa2 location","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code","def":"A 9-digit hierarchical code under ASGS Edition 3: one digit for state or territory, two for SA4, two for SA3 and four for the SA2 within it. There are 2,473 SA2s, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes such as Migratory, Offshore and Shipping and No Usual Address.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","lim":"An SA2 averages about 10,000 residents, coarse enough to hide differences inside a suburb yet fine enough that a count of outlets in one SA2 can point at a single provider. It describes the outlet's own community, not its catchment, and sessions delivered by telephone, video or online are still reported against it however far away the client was.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"],"dom":28},{"n":"SA22016BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The 2016-vintage SA2 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address, holding the client's suburb-scale location on special_client and the outlet's on special_outlet.","full":"The 2016-vintage SA2 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address, holding the client's suburb-scale location on special_client and the outlet's on special_outlet. SA2 is the level at which Data Exchange activity is usually set against ABS population and socio-economic measures, because it is the finest level most non-Census ABS statistics are published at. The 2011, 2016 and 2021 SA2 columns sit side by side in the curated Data Exchange client table, one per Census edition.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Client Address: SA2 2016 Boundary Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 2 code","def":"A 9-digit code on the ASGS July 2016 edition, hierarchical from state through SA4 and SA3 to the SA2. It is also the first nine digits of the 11-digit SA1 code, so the SA2 can be read off the SA1 column on the same row.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","lim":"Vintage and geocoder both matter here: this is the 2016 boundary set produced by the DSS address validation service, so it will not reconcile with the ABS-coded SA2_ASGS_2021 on special_outlet, and a mismatch between the two is not evidence that anything moved. An address that failed validation carries no code rather than a wrong one, so missingness is concentrated in poorly recorded addresses.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"SA22021BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The 2021-vintage SA2 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address, for the client on special_client and for the outlet on special_outlet.","full":"The 2021-vintage SA2 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address, for the client on special_client and for the outlet on special_outlet. It is the level most analyses of Data Exchange geography settle on, because it is fine enough to be locally meaningful and coarse enough to publish without identifying a provider or a client. Where the analysis needs the outlet's ABS-derived geography instead, SA2_ASGS_2021 on the outlet table is the equivalent column.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Client Address: SA2 2021 Boundary Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code","def":"A 9-digit hierarchical code under ASGS Edition 3, July 2021 to June 2026. There are 2,473 SA2s, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes for populations that cannot be placed, such as No Usual Address.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","lim":"For a client this is the geography of the address on file, which the protocols allow to be a substitute: a homeless client's record may hold the suburb where they usually sleep or the suburb of the outlet, and a client at risk of family violence may have the outlet's address recorded instead of their own. Reading client SA2 counts as a map of where clients live therefore pulls people towards the suburbs where services sit.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"],"dom":28},{"n":"SA32016BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The 2016-vintage SA3 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address on the client or outlet record.","full":"The 2016-vintage SA3 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address on the client or outlet record. SA3s group SA2s into regions of roughly 30,000 to 130,000 people, which is the scale at which service coverage across a district can be described without exposing an individual provider. Note the asymmetry on special_outlet: it carries SA3 boundary codes from the DSS geocoder, but the ABS-coded block on that table has no SA3 column, running from SA2_ASGS_2021 straight to SA4_ASGS_2021.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Client Address: SA3 2016 Boundary Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 3 code","def":"A 5-digit hierarchical code on the ASGS July 2016 edition: one digit for state or territory, two for SA4 and two for the SA3 within it. It is also the first five digits of the SA1 and SA2 codes on the same row.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","lim":"SA3s are drawn for regional statistical output and deliberately ignore local government and service catchment boundaries, so an SA3 tally will not match a council's own figures or a program's funded region. The 2016 and 2021 SA3 sets differ in both number and shape, so the two boundary code columns cannot be pooled.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"SA32021BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The 2021-vintage SA3 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address, on both the client and the outlet records.","full":"The 2021-vintage SA3 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address, on both the client and the outlet records. It is the middle rung of the boundary code family, the level at which many DSS program reports are published because it survives disclosure control while still describing a recognisable district. There is no ABS-coded SA3 column in this product, so this is the only SA3 available for the 2021 vintage.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 3","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-3","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Client Address: SA3 2021 Boundary Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 3 code","def":"A 5-digit hierarchical code under ASGS Edition 3: one digit for state or territory, two for SA4 and two for the SA3. There are 359 SA3s, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 3","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-3","lim":"An SA3 is large enough that services anywhere across a whole city fringe look identical, so using it as the analytical unit throws away the SA1 and SA2 detail on the same row for no gain unless disclosure requires it. It is also not a program boundary: DSS funded activity regions and SA3s do not align.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"SA4_ASGS_2021","d":"The SA4 the service outlet sits in, coded by ABS from the address register match, and the coarsest sub-state level in the ABS block on this table.","full":"The SA4 the service outlet sits in, coded by ABS from the address register match, and the coarsest sub-state level in the ABS block on this table. ABS describes SA4s as \"geographic areas built from whole Statistical Areas Level 3 (SA3s)\" that are \"the largest sub-state regions in the Main Structure of the ASGS\", with boundaries drawn to represent labour markets. Because Labour Force estimates are published at SA4, this is the column that lets outlet activity be read against regional unemployment and participation.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 4","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-4","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Sa4 location","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 4 code","def":"A 3-digit code: a one-digit state or territory identifier followed by a two-digit SA4 identifier unique within that state, as in 102 for Central Coast. There are 108 SA4s under ASGS Edition 3, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes, and the four Other Territories share a single SA4.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 4","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-4","lim":"SA4s hold between 100,000 and 500,000 people and exist to support Labour Force sampling, not service planning, so they are far too coarse to show where a service is needed. The count also changed between editions, from 107 in the 2016 ASGS to 108 in Edition 3, so a series that crosses the change needs a concordance rather than a direct join.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"SA42016BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The 2016-vintage SA4 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address.","full":"The 2016-vintage SA4 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address. For an outlet DSS defines it as \"the designated region representing geographical areas built up from Statistical Areas Level 3 (SA3s) in order to allow for the output of a variety of regional data that a given outlet's physical address is located within, as represented by a code\", and the same column on special_client does the same job for the client's residential address. It is stored as a three-character value rather than a number.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Outlet: Physical Address, Statistical Area Level 4 (SA4) Code (ASGS 2016) N(3)', Aristotle item 1511","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1511","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Client Address: SA4 2016 Boundary Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 4 code","def":"A 3-digit code on the ASGS July 2016 edition: one digit for state or territory then two for the SA4 within it. DSS records that the 2016 edition has 107 SA4 regions, including 18 non-spatial special purpose codes for Migratory, Offshore and Shipping and for No Usual Address in each state, with the Other Territories represented by a single SA4.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Outlet: Physical Address, Statistical Area Level 4 (SA4) Code (ASGS 2016) N(3)', Aristotle item 1511","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1511","lim":"An SA4 is a labour market region, so it tells you which regional labour market an address sits in and nothing about the neighbourhood around it. The 2016 set has one fewer region than the 2021 set and several boundaries were redrawn, so the two SA4 boundary columns on a row will disagree in places where nothing physically moved.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"SA42021BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The 2021-vintage SA4 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address, the coarsest boundary code below state.","full":"The 2021-vintage SA4 the DSS geocoder assigned to the address, the coarsest boundary code below state. It is the level most Data Exchange output lands on when results have to be published without disclosing a small provider, since each SA4 covers at least about 100,000 residents. On special_outlet it describes the same premises as SA4_ASGS_2021, but the two come from different geocoding paths and are not guaranteed to agree.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, value domain 'Statistical area level 4 (SA4) code (ASGS 2021)', Aristotle item 108924","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108924","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Client Address: SA4 2021 Boundary Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 4 code","def":"A code for an ASGS Edition 3 SA4 region, of which there are 108. DSS registers its own SA4 (ASGS 2021) domain with a four-character format and a supplementary value of 9 for default, against the three digits ABS uses, so check the stored width before joining to an ABS-coded SA4 column.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, value domain 'Statistical area level 4 (SA4) code (ASGS 2021)', Aristotle item 108924","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/108924","lim":"A disagreement between this column and SA4_ASGS_2021 is a geocoding difference, not a boundary change, so taking either as authoritative without checking will quietly move outlets between regions. The column also cannot support labour market analysis of clients, because it locates an address, while an SA4's labour market meaning rests on where people work.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"]},{"n":"SCOREID","d":"The identifier of one domain rating inside a SCORE assessment, defined by DSS as \"a system-generated identifier for a unique outcome domain assessment record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number\".","full":"The identifier of one domain rating inside a SCORE assessment, defined by DSS as \"a system-generated identifier for a unique outcome domain assessment record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number\". A single assessment, identified by ASSESSMENTID, can rate several outcome domains at once, so special_client_assessment holds one row per SCOREID and several SCOREIDs per assessment, each with its own OUTCOMEDOMAIN and OUTCOMEDOMAINSCORE. This is therefore the row key: counting assessments means counting distinct ASSESSMENTID values, not rows.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client_Assessment (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Data Exchange: Outcome domain assessment identifier, ID number', Aristotle item 1709","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1709","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A system-generated identifier for a unique outcome domain assessment record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.","k":"DEX outcome domain assessment identifier","def":"A system-generated number of up to 19 digits, registered in the curated Data Exchange client assessment table with the format N[N(18)]. It carries no meaning in itself and is not comparable across the client and community assessment tables.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, Client_Assessment (DEX Curated) distribution, data element 'Data Exchange: Outcome domain assessment identifier, ID number', Aristotle item 1709","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1709","lim":"It identifies a rating, not an outcome. SCOREs are designed to be reported in pairs, an initial rating near the start of service and a subsequent one later, and the pairing is made on the domain across assessments, so one SCOREID on its own shows a level and never a change. Nor does it say who did the rating, which ASSESSEDBY and ASSESSEDBYCODE carry.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment"]},{"n":"SERVICESETTINGCODE","d":"Where or how a session was actually delivered, which DSS defines as \"the category of physical location or delivery method for a given session, represented by a label\".","full":"Where or how a session was actually delivered, which DSS defines as \"the category of physical location or delivery method for a given session, represented by a label\". It is the correction to OUTLETID: the outlet is where staff are based, while this column separates a session held in the office from one at the client's home, a community venue, a partner organisation, a health, education or justice facility, or one delivered by telephone, video or online. For any question about outreach models or about the shift to remote delivery, this is the column that holds the answer.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Session: Service setting, Label', Aristotle item 1331","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1331","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Where services are provided, represented by a label. E.g. Organisation outlet, Community venue, telephone etc.","t":"categorical","k":"DEX service setting label","def":"An uppercase label of up to 15 characters. The registry's permissible values, in force from 18 August 2018, are ORGOUTLETOFFICE, CLRES, COMMVENUE, PARORG, TELE, DIGITAL, HEALTHFACILITY, EDUFACILITY and JUSTICEFACILITY; the March 2024 protocols describe Telephone, Video and Online service as three separate settings where the registry carries the single DIGITAL value beside TELE.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Session: Service setting, Label', Aristotle item 1331","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1331","lim":"It is optional extended data, so a blank is not an office visit. Only one setting is recorded per session, so a service that began on the phone and finished in person appears as whichever the organisation judged dominant. It also describes the delivery channel, not the client's whereabouts: a telephone session says nothing about where the client was sitting.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"],"dom":29},{"n":"SERVICETYPEID","d":"The kind of help delivered, defined by DSS as \"the main focus of service delivery at a given session, represented by a code\".","full":"The kind of help delivered, defined by DSS as \"the main focus of service delivery at a given session, represented by a code\". The codes begin at 1 for intake or assessment and 2 for information, advice and referral, and continue through education and skills training, child and youth focused groups, counselling and dispute resolution. Which of them an organisation may use depends on the program activity, because the Data Exchange portal offers only the service types attached to the activity being reported, and special_service_type is the lookup that gives each code its name.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Session: Service type, Code', Aristotle item 1289","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1289","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The main focus of service delivery related to a given attendance, represented by a number.","k":"DEX service type code","def":"A number of up to three digits from a single registry-wide list dating from 20 June 2014. The list is long, and the subset available for any one program activity is published in that program's guidance rather than in the protocols.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Session: Service type, Code', Aristotle item 1289","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1289","lim":"Only one service type is recorded per session, so the column understates what a session contained: counselling that also arranged a referral is recorded as counselling alone, on the protocols' rule that the type taking most of the time or achieving the outcome wins. The codes are shared across programs but the menus are not, so a national count by service type mixes activities that use one code for quite different work.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_service_type","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"SESSIONCONDUCTEDDATE","d":"The date of the session a SCORE assessment relates to, defined by DSS as \"the date a given session took place, represented by DDMMYYYY\".","full":"The date of the session a SCORE assessment relates to, defined by DSS as \"the date a given session took place, represented by DDMMYYYY\". On the assessment tables it is the anchor for ordering initial and subsequent ratings, and it is the date that decides which reporting period the assessment counts against, unlike SESSIONCREATEDDATE and ASSESSMENTCREATEDDATE, which record when the record was keyed in. CONDUCTEDDATE on special_attendance carries the same fact for attendance rows.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Session: Conducted date, DDMMYYYY', Aristotle item 890","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/890","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The date on which a given session occurred recorded as the day of a particular month and year.","k":"date","def":"A calendar date at day resolution, registered in DDMMYYYY form with no time component. The protocols require session dates to be entered as dd/mm/yyyy.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Session: Conducted date, DDMMYYYY', Aristotle item 890","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/890","lim":"The date belongs to the session, not to the assessment, so several ratings, several domains and several clients share one value and it cannot order two assessments made on the same day. DSS notes that since 18 August 2018 the service phase label is no longer the primary means of ordering assessments either. It also dates the rating, never the change in circumstances being rated.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment"]},{"n":"SESSIONCREATEDDATE","d":"When the session record was first entered into the Data Exchange, as against SESSIONCONDUCTEDDATE, which is when the session happened.","full":"When the session record was first entered into the Data Exchange, as against SESSIONCONDUCTEDDATE, which is when the session happened. The gap between the two is reporting lag: organisations may enter data at any point in a six-month reporting period and for 30 days after it closes, so a session held in January can be created in August. Use it to judge how current the data was and to spot bulk loads, never to date the service.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Created date, DDMMYYYY', Aristotle item 1672, the created-date element registered for this table","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1672","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"The date and time at which the session record was first created in DEX","k":"record creation timestamp","def":"A date and time stamped by the system when the record was written. The sibling element on this table, ASSESSMENTCREATEDDATE, is registered as the date a record \"was entered into a system\" in DDMMYYYY form, so expect day resolution at best from the date part.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Client outcome assessment: Created date, DDMMYYYY', Aristotle item 1672, the created-date element registered for this table","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1672","lim":"It dates the record, not the event, and it is a system value rather than a service fact: a bulk upload creates thousands of session records within one second, and a system migration can restamp records that describe much older sessions. A long gap from the conducted date is a sign of late reporting, not of a long service.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment"]},{"n":"SESSIONID","d":"The key of a single instance of service, which DSS defines as \"a system-generated identifier for a unique session record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number\".","full":"The key of a single instance of service, which DSS defines as \"a system-generated identifier for a unique session record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number\". The protocols define a session as an individual episode of service stored within a case, and this is the column that holds the session tables together: special_session has one row per session, special_attendance one row per person present, and the assessment tables hang their SCOREs off the same value. Organisations uploading in bulk supply their own session identifier, and the Data Exchange generates one only when the portal field is left blank.","dsrc":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Data Exchange: Session identifier, ID number', Aristotle item 1775","durl":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1775","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"A system-generated identifier for a unique session record in the Data Exchange, represented by a number.","k":"DEX session identifier","def":"A number of up to 19 digits, registered with the format N[N(18)]. It is unique within the case rather than globally meaningful, and the identifier the provider supplied is limited to 50 characters before the Data Exchange converts it.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Metadata Registry, data element 'Data Exchange: Session identifier, ID number', Aristotle item 1775","url":"https://dss.aristotlecloud.io/item/1775","lim":"A session is a reporting construct, not a unit of effort: a two-hour group workshop and a five-minute phone call are each one session, so session counts are not workload and ASSISTANCEMINUTES is the column for that. The curated attendance table also writes aggregate rows for unidentified clients using the negative of the session identifier as the attendance key, so naive counts of attendance identifiers within a session can be thrown out by those rows.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"SOURCESYSTEMCODE","d":"Code to identify source system for the activity (e.g. FOFMS, EXTNL)","vp":"ai","od":"Code to identify source system for the activity (e.g. FOFMS, EXTNL)","k":"dex_source_system (inferred)","def":"The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"guessed","src":"Inferred from the variable name and description","lim":"The value domain is inferred from the variable name and description, not published by the source. The values are of the right shape but are not a confirmed mapping.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_activity"]},{"n":"STARTDATE","d":"When a service activity became available to deliver, not when anybody received it.","full":"When a service activity became available to deliver, not when anybody received it. The Data Exchange models a funded service as an activity with an availability window, and clients attach to it through separate session records, so this is a property of the funding arrangement. Using it as a service start date for a client attributes the whole activity's lifetime to everyone who touched it.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/document/501","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"The date that a given activity is available for service.","k":"Activity availability start date","def":"The domain is open, so no finite value list applies.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/document/501","lim":"The date belongs to the activity, not to any client, and says nothing about when service was actually delivered. The domain is inferred from the DIL wording; the Data Exchange publishes its protocols but not this field's definition.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_activity"]},{"n":"STATE_ASGS_2021","d":"The state or territory of the outlet's address as ABS coded it under ASGS Edition 3, and the top of the hierarchy the SA1, SA2 and SA4 columns beside it belong to.","full":"The state or territory of the outlet's address as ABS coded it under ASGS Edition 3, and the top of the hierarchy the SA1, SA2 and SA4 columns beside it belong to. ABS records that \"in general, the total area of each State and Territory, including their offshore islands, is used for statistical purposes as a separate geographic area in the ASGS\". OUTLETSTATE on the same row is the state the organisation typed in, so the two can disagree wherever the entered address was wrong or out of date, and this one follows the geocoded address.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Australia and State/Territory","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/australia-and-stateterritory","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"State (number)","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS 2021 state and territory code","def":"A one-digit code: 1 New South Wales, 2 Victoria, 3 Queensland, 4 South Australia, 5 Western Australia, 6 Tasmania, 7 Northern Territory, 8 Australian Capital Territory and 9 Other Territories. It is also the leading digit of the SA1, SA2 and SA4 codes on the same row, so the three are internally consistent by construction.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Australia and State/Territory","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/australia-and-stateterritory","lim":"Code 9 is a bundle rather than a place: Jervis Bay Territory and the Christmas Island, Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island territories are one category and cannot be separated. The value also describes the premises, so a national help line run from one office puts all of its sessions in a single jurisdiction, which is a poor basis for comparing service levels between states.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"],"dom":6},{"n":"STE2016BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The state or territory the DSS geocoder derived from the address on the record, on the 2016 ASGS boundaries: the client's residence on special_client and the outlet's premises on special_outlet.","full":"The state or territory the DSS geocoder derived from the address on the record, on the 2016 ASGS boundaries: the client's residence on special_client and the outlet's premises on special_outlet. Of the whole boundary code family this is the one that almost never changes between vintages, which makes it the safest fallback when a finer code failed to resolve. The curated Data Exchange client table carries the 2011, 2016 and 2021 state codes side by side.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Client Address: 2016 State Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS 2016 state and territory code","def":"A one-digit code from 1 to 9 on the ASGS July 2016 edition, with 9 covering the Other Territories.
