It is the leading digit of the SA1, SA2, SA3 and SA4 boundary codes on the same row, so it can be derived from any of them.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","lim":"State boundaries barely move, so a row where the 2016 and 2021 state codes differ is evidence of an address edit or a geocoding change rather than of a boundary revision, and treating the pair as a migration signal will produce false moves. For a client, the state is the state of the address recorded, which the protocols allow to be the outlet's address where the client is homeless or at risk.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"],"dom":6},{"n":"STE2021BOUNDARYCODE","d":"The state or territory of the address on ASGS Edition 3 boundaries, assigned by the DSS geocoder to the client record and to the outlet record.","full":"The state or territory of the address on ASGS Edition 3 boundaries, assigned by the DSS geocoder to the client record and to the outlet record. It is the coarsest of the 2021 boundary codes and the one most Data Exchange program reporting is broken down by, because activities are commissioned jurisdiction by jurisdiction. On special_outlet it should agree with STATE_ASGS_2021, which ABS derived independently through the address register match.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Australia and State/Territory","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/australia-and-stateterritory","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Client Address: 2021 State Code boundary tagged by DSS IQ Office (Address Validation and Geocoder service)","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS 2021 state and territory code","def":"A one-digit code from 1 to 9 under ASGS Edition 3, July 2021 to June 2026, where 9 is Other Territories. Australia itself is coded AUS in Edition 3, replacing the numeric 036 used in the 2016 edition.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Australia and State/Territory","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/australia-and-stateterritory","lim":"It does not identify who funds or administers the service. DSS is a Commonwealth department, several Data Exchange program values belong to state agencies, and a client's state and the funding jurisdiction are separate questions. Nor is it a reliable statement of usual residence: a client can move between service episodes without the address on their record being updated.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet"],"dom":6},{"n":"SYNTHETIC_AEUID","d":"The person key that runs through the Data Exchange tables: one client carries the same value across special_client, special_attendance, special_client_assessment, special_client_disability and special_community_assessment, which is what turns scattered session rows into a service history.","full":"The person key that runs through the Data Exchange tables: one client carries the same value across special_client, special_attendance, special_client_assessment, special_client_disability and special_community_assessment, which is what turns scattered session rows into a service history. It is the DSS client identifier in anonymised form, not a PLIDA-wide person number: ABS links datasets through a \"Person Linkage Spine\" held \"separate from the main body of data\", so joining a Data Exchange client to their Medicare, tax or payment records means going out through the agency spine file to the spine identifier and back in through another agency's identifier.","dsrc":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/about/data-services/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Anonymised DEX person level id","k":"PLIDA agency person identifier (anonymised)","def":"An opaque identifier with no internal structure and no decodable content. It is stable within the DSS extract and meaningless outside it, so it can be compared for equality and nothing else.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/about/data-services/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida","lim":"It identifies a client record, not a person. The Data Exchange creates client records at the delivery organisation level, so someone who registers with two providers under different details can hold two identifiers until the statistical linkage key brings them together. Linkage to the PLIDA spine also fails for a share of records, and an unlinked client is missing from the other datasets rather than absent from them.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_attendance","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_disability","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment"]},{"n":"SYSENDTIME","d":"The moment this version of the row stopped being the current one.","full":"The moment this version of the row stopped being the current one. The seven reference tables that carry it — activity, client, client disability, organisation, outlet, program and service type — are delivered as full row histories rather than snapshots, and SYSSTARTTIME and SYSENDTIME bound the window in which each version was live. The current version carries the maximum value the type allows rather than a null, so the filter for a snapshot is SYSENDTIME at its maximum, or equivalently CURRENTRECORD set to 1.","dsrc":"Microsoft, SQL Server temporal tables documentation, which defines the SysStartTime and SysEndTime period columns this pair follows","durl":"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/tables/temporal-tables","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Record end date and time","k":"system-versioning period end timestamp","def":"A datetime in UTC closing a version's period. Following the system-versioned temporal table convention the columns are named for, the open row is given 9999-12-31 23:59:59.9999999 rather than a null, so comparisons against a null will silently drop the current record.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"Microsoft, SQL Server temporal tables documentation, which defines the SysStartTime and SysEndTime period columns this pair follows","url":"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/tables/temporal-tables","lim":"It records when the database row was superseded, not when the thing it describes ended: an outlet that closed in March but was edited in September ends its version in September. ENDDATE on special_activity is the service fact — the date an activity is no longer available for service — while this column is only the record's lifetime in the system.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_activity","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_disability","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_organisation","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_program","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_service_type"]},{"n":"SYSSTARTTIME","d":"The moment this version of the row became current.","full":"The moment this version of the row became current. Reading any of the seven reference tables without filtering on it counts one outlet, client or activity several times over, because the product ships every version of every reference record rather than a snapshot. Paired with SYSENDTIME it gives the window in which the row was live, and RECORDSEQNBR numbers the same versions in the same order. A record that has never been edited has one version, whose start time is when it was first written.","dsrc":"Microsoft, SQL Server temporal tables documentation, which defines the SysStartTime and SysEndTime period columns this pair follows","durl":"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/tables/temporal-tables","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Record start date and time","k":"system-versioning period start timestamp","def":"A datetime in UTC opening the period during which this version was current. Under the system-versioned convention the columns are named for, one version's end time equals the next version's start time, so the periods abut exactly and leave no gaps in an entity's history.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"Microsoft, SQL Server temporal tables documentation, which defines the SysStartTime and SysEndTime period columns this pair follows","url":"https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/tables/temporal-tables","lim":"It is a database write time, so it dates the data entry rather than the event: a client record created in 2019 that describes services from 2016 carries a 2019 start time. It also cannot be read across tables as a measure of when anything happened, because a bulk load stamps thousands of unrelated rows with a single time.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_activity","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_disability","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_organisation","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_outlet","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_program","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_service_type"]},{"n":"THEDATE","d":"The calendar date a Data Exchange calendar-table row stands for.","full":"The calendar date a Data Exchange calendar-table row stands for. Every other column on the row is derived from it: THEDAY, THEDAYNAME, THEDAYOFWEEK, THEWEEK, THEISOWEEK, THEMONTH, THEQUARTER, THEYEAR and THEFINANCIALYEAR, with THEREPORTINGPERIOD and REPORTINGPERIODENDTIME placing it in one of the two six-monthly reporting periods. It exists so a session's conducted date can be joined to consistent period labels rather than each analyst deriving their own, which matters because the protocols count a session against a reporting period by its date.","dsrc":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, sections 3.4 and 10.3","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"calendar date","def":"A calendar date at day resolution and the primary key of special_ref_calendar, with one row for every day the table spans, weekends and public holidays included.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS, The Data Exchange Protocols, Version 11, March 2024, sections 3.4 and 10.3","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"The table describes the calendar, not the data: a date is present whether or not any session occurred on it, so counting rows here measures the span of the calendar and never activity. Joining to it cannot fill gaps either — a day with no sessions simply produces no match on the other side of the join.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THEDAY","d":"The day-of-month number for one row of the Data Exchange calendar, which holds one row per date rather than one row per client or service.","full":"The day-of-month number for one row of the Data Exchange calendar, which holds one row per date rather than one row per client or service. The calendar exists because everything in the Data Exchange is counted by the date of a session, so THEDATE on the same row is the date itself and THEDAY, THEMONTH and THEYEAR are its parts, pre-computed for joining and grouping. Nothing on this row belongs to a person, an outlet or an organisation.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"day of month, 1 to 31","def":"A whole number from 1 to 31, the day component of the Gregorian date held in THEDATE on the same row. It is a calendar attribute, not a duration and not a count.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"The number cannot order or identify a date on its own, because the 3rd of one month and the 3rd of the next share a value, so grouping by it pools every month together. It also tells you nothing about service delivery until the calendar table is joined to a session or assessment table on the date.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THEDAYNAME","d":"The name of the weekday for one row of the Data Exchange calendar, spelled out rather than numbered.","full":"The name of the weekday for one row of the Data Exchange calendar, spelled out rather than numbered. THEDAYOFWEEK beside it carries the same fact as an index, so the two never disagree and only one of them is needed. Joined to the session tables it answers whether a funded activity was delivered on weekends, which differs sharply between family services and emergency relief.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"weekday name","def":"A weekday label in English, one of the seven names from Monday to Sunday, derived from the date in THEDATE on the same row.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"A weekday label says nothing about whether an outlet was open, whether the day was a public holiday, or whether staff worked it, because the Data Exchange holds no opening hours or holiday calendar. Session dates are also often entered in bulk well after the event, so an unlikely-looking day pattern can be a data-entry habit rather than a delivery pattern.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THEDAYOFWEEK","d":"Calendar related data fields","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"day of week index, 1-7 (inferred)","def":"The values are inferred from the variable name and description, not published by the source.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"guessed","src":"Inferred from the variable name and description","lim":"The value domain is inferred from the variable name and description, not published by the source. The values are of the right shape but are not a confirmed mapping.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"],"dom":30},{"n":"THEDAYOFYEAR","d":"The position of the date within its calendar year, counting 1 January as day one.","full":"The position of the date within its calendar year, counting 1 January as day one. On the Data Exchange calendar it is the attribute that lets service volumes be lined up across years without month boundaries getting in the way, which is how seasonal demand for emergency relief or financial counselling is usually looked at. It is a property of the date alone and repeats identically for every year in the table.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"day of year, 1 to 366","def":"A whole number from 1 to 365, or to 366 in a leap year, counted from 1 January of the year in THEYEAR on the same row.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"The number does not map to the same calendar date in every year: after February a leap year shifts everything by one, so aligning years on this column misaligns the dates by a day. It also cuts across the Data Exchange reporting cycle, which runs in six-month halves from 1 July, so a day-of-year series cannot be tied back to a reporting period without THEREPORTINGPERIOD.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THEFINANCIALYEAR","d":"The July-to-June year the date falls in, which is the year Data Exchange funding agreements and performance reporting run on.","full":"The July-to-June year the date falls in, which is the year Data Exchange funding agreements and performance reporting run on. The Quick Start Guide sets the cycle out as two halves: \"There are two reporting periods per year which run from 1 July to 31 December and 1 January to 30 June, with a 30 day close off period to allow you to finalise your data.\" This column names the pair of halves taken together, while THEREPORTINGPERIOD on the same row names which half.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Quick Start Guide (April 2020), 'Start entering data'","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2022-07/1391-data-exchange-quick-start.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"Australian financial year, 1 July to 30 June","def":"A year label rather than a date: the year beginning 1 July and ending 30 June that contains the date in THEDATE, conventionally written as the two calendar years it spans.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Quick Start Guide (April 2020), 'Start entering data'","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2022-07/1391-data-exchange-quick-start.pdf","lim":"It is not the calendar year in THEYEAR, and the two disagree for every date between January and June, so mixing them splits a single year of activity across two labels. It also says nothing about whether the reporting period was still open when a record was entered, because organisations have a further 30 days after each half closes.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THEFIRSTOFMONTH","d":"The first date of the month that contains this calendar row's date, held as a date so it can be used directly as a monthly grouping key.","full":"The first date of the month that contains this calendar row's date, held as a date so it can be used directly as a monthly grouping key. Every date in the same month carries the same value, which is what makes it useful for building a monthly series of sessions or assessments without truncating dates in the query. THELASTOFYEAR beside it does the same job at the other end of the year.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"date of the first day of the month","def":"A date, always the 1st of the month, derived from the date in THEDATE on the same row.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"The value is a label for a month, not an event date, so a row carrying 1 March is no evidence that anything happened on 1 March. Monthly grouping built on it also cannot be reconciled with published Data Exchange figures, which are produced for six-month reporting periods rather than months.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THEISOWEEK","d":"The ISO 8601 week that this calendar row's date falls in, kept separately from THEWEEK because the two count weeks by different rules.","full":"The ISO 8601 week that this calendar row's date falls in, kept separately from THEWEEK because the two count weeks by different rules. Under ISO 8601 a week runs Monday to Sunday and week 1 is the week containing the first Thursday of the year, so the ISO week is the one to use when weekly service counts have to line up with any external weekly series. Joined to the session tables it gives a weekly view of delivery inside a six-month reporting period.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"ISO 8601 week","def":"An ISO 8601 week identifier: a week number from 1 to 53 within an ISO week-numbering year, which is not always the calendar year of the date.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"Late December and early January dates commonly fall in an ISO week belonging to the neighbouring year, so grouping by this column together with THEYEAR splits one week across two rows and produces a short week at each year end. The column also cannot be matched against THEWEEK, which numbers weeks on a different rule.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THELASTOFYEAR","d":"The last date of the calendar year that contains this row's date, held as a date and repeated for every day of that year.","full":"The last date of the calendar year that contains this row's date, held as a date and repeated for every day of that year. It is a grouping and alignment key, the year-end counterpart of THEFIRSTOFMONTH, and it is a calendar year end rather than anything to do with Data Exchange reporting. REPORTINGPERIODENDTIME on the same calendar row is the field that carries the end of the reporting period.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 10.3 reporting periods and deadlines","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"date of the last day of the calendar year","def":"A date, always 31 December, derived from the year of the date in THEDATE on the same row.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 10.3 reporting periods and deadlines","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"It is easily mistaken for a period end: Data Exchange reporting periods close on 31 December and 30 June, so for half the year this column points at a date that is not the relevant deadline at all. It is also not a financial year end, which falls on 30 June.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THEMONTH","d":"The calendar month number for this row of the Data Exchange calendar.","full":"The calendar month number for this row of the Data Exchange calendar. THEMONTHNAME holds the same fact as text and THEQUARTER groups it into quarters, so the three are alternative levels of the same monthly hierarchy rather than separate pieces of information. Joined to sessions it is the usual way to look at within-year movement in service volumes.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"calendar month number, 1 to 12","def":"A whole number from 1 to 12, where 1 is January, taken from the date in THEDATE on the same row.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"The number does not identify a month in time: it repeats every year, so grouping by it alone pools every January in the collection into one figure. It also starts the year in January, while Data Exchange activity is funded and reported from July, so a run of months 1 to 12 crosses two reporting cycles.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THEMONTHNAME","d":"The month spelled out in words for this row of the Data Exchange calendar, provided so reports can be labelled without converting a number.","full":"The month spelled out in words for this row of the Data Exchange calendar, provided so reports can be labelled without converting a number. It duplicates THEMONTH on the same row, which carries the month as a number, and the two are never inconsistent. Nothing about the funded activity, the outlet or the client is recorded here.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"month name","def":"A month label in English, one of the twelve names from January to December, derived from the date in THEDATE on the same row.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"Being text, it sorts alphabetically rather than chronologically, so a report ordered on this column starts at April and ends at September; order on THEMONTH instead. Like the month number it also repeats across years and cannot identify a particular month without THEYEAR.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THEQUARTER","d":"The calendar quarter this row's date falls in, numbered from the March quarter.","full":"The calendar quarter this row's date falls in, numbered from the March quarter. It is a coarser level of the same hierarchy as THEMONTH and THEMONTHNAME, and it is a calendar quarter rather than a quarter of the Data Exchange year, which starts in July. Two quarters make one Data Exchange reporting period, so the column can split a period in half but never straddles one.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 10.3 reporting periods and deadlines","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"calendar quarter, 1 to 4","def":"A whole number from 1 to 4, where 1 covers January to March, derived from the date in THEDATE on the same row.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 10.3 reporting periods and deadlines","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"Quarterly totals built on this column cannot be reconciled with any published Data Exchange figure, because the collection reports in six-month periods and never in quarters. Quarter 1 is also the January to March quarter, not the first quarter of the funding year, which is July to September.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THEREPORTINGPERIOD","d":"The six-month performance period a record is counted against, which is the unit the whole Data Exchange is reported in.","full":"The six-month performance period a record is counted against, which is the unit the whole Data Exchange is reported in. The Quick Start Guide states that \"There are two reporting periods per year which run from 1 July to 31 December and 1 January to 30 June, with a 30 day close off period to allow you to finalise your data.\" On the calendar table it maps any date to its period; on the client and community assessment tables it names the period in which the session being assessed was conducted, which is how a SCORE assessment is attributed. The Protocols add the counting rule: a session belongs to a period if the session date fell inside it and at least one client is attached.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Quick Start Guide (April 2020), 'Start entering data'; DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), sections 3.4 and 10.3","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2022-07/1391-data-exchange-quick-start.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The Reporting Period in which a session was conducted.","k":"Data Exchange six-month reporting period","def":"A six-month period label covering either 1 July to 31 December or 1 January to 30 June. REPORTINGPERIODENDTIME on the same calendar row carries the closing date of that period.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Quick Start Guide (April 2020), 'Start entering data'; DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), sections 3.4 and 10.3","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2022-07/1391-data-exchange-quick-start.pdf","lim":"The period says when a service is counted, not when it was recorded: organisations may enter data at any time during the period and for 30 days after it closes, and later still if the department grants a system re-opening, so this is not a measure of data currency. A case with sessions in both halves of the year is counted in both periods, so summing counts by period double counts continuing clients and cases.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_client_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_community_assessment","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THEWEEK","d":"The week of the year this row's date falls in, numbered on the warehouse's own rule rather than the ISO rule.","full":"The week of the year this row's date falls in, numbered on the warehouse's own rule rather than the ISO rule. It exists alongside THEISOWEEK precisely because the two differ: a calendar table carries both so that a report can pick the convention it needs. Joined to the session tables it supports weekly delivery counts within a reporting period.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"week of year number","def":"A week number within the calendar year, running from 1 to 53 or 54 depending on where the year starts in the week.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 3.4 counting rules for clients, cases and sessions","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"The rule for the first and last weeks of the year is not published, so a week 1 may be a part week of one or two days and week counts are not comparable across years. Values here also cannot be matched to the ISO week numbers in THEISOWEEK, which start weeks on Monday and place week 1 differently.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"THEYEAR","d":"The calendar year of this row's date on the Data Exchange calendar.","full":"The calendar year of this row's date on the Data Exchange calendar. It is the coarsest level of the calendar hierarchy and the one most often joined to sessions for an annual series, but it is the January-to-December year, not the funding year the collection is built around. THEFINANCIALYEAR on the same row holds the July-to-June year, and THEREPORTINGPERIOD holds the six-month half.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 10.3 reporting periods and deadlines","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Calendar related data fields","k":"calendar year","def":"A four-digit Gregorian year taken from the date in THEDATE on the same row.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 10.3 reporting periods and deadlines","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"An annual count grouped on this column will not match any published Data Exchange or departmental figure, because those run from July to June; each calendar year mixes the second half of one funding year with the first half of the next. It also cannot be combined with THEISOWEEK without splitting the week that spans the year end.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_calendar"]},{"n":"TOPICCODE","d":"The advocacy issue a National Disability Advocacy Program session was about, recorded on the session record.","full":"The advocacy issue a National Disability Advocacy Program session was about, recorded on the session record. The Protocols describe the item as captured at the session level, where \"This field allows organisations to select the reason why a client is accessing a service\", and make it mandatory only for that program. The published list is of advocacy issues rather than service types: abuse, neglect and violence, discrimination and rights, NDIS access and planning, housing and homelessness, legal access to justice, transport, and about a dozen more. It sits beside SERVICETYPEID, which records what was delivered, while this records what it was about.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 5.3.4 and Table 14, National Disability Advocacy Program session level data","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"This field descibes the reason why a client is accessing a service, represented by a label.","t":"categorical","k":"National Disability Advocacy Program session topic","def":"One label from a closed list of about twenty advocacy issues published in Table 14 of the Protocols. Despite the column name the stored value is the label text, not a number.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 5.3.4 and Table 14, National Disability Advocacy Program session level data","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"Only one topic is recorded per session, so a session that dealt with a housing problem and a payment problem shows one of them and the other is invisible. The field is collected only for National Disability Advocacy Program activities, so an empty value almost always means a different program rather than an unknown reason, and it must not be read as a diagnosis, a disability type or an outcome.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"],"dom":31},{"n":"TRAINING","d":"A marker that education and skills training was one of the domains recorded for a client, set on two different reference tables.","full":"A marker that education and skills training was one of the domains recorded for a client, set on two different reference tables. On the reasons-for-assistance table it flags the reason category the Protocols define as \"Education and skills training: where the client is seeking to engage with education and skills training to improve their independence, participation and wellbeing\"; on the referral table it flags a referral made for that purpose. The columns beside it, HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, MENTAL, MONEY, PERSONAL and the rest, are the other domains from the same list, and several can be set on one row because a client can present with more than one need.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 6.2 reasons for seeking assistance and section 6.4 referrals to other services","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Seeking assistance related to skills training","k":"education and skills training domain flag","def":"A yes-or-no indicator rather than a code, one column per domain on a reference row keyed by ASSISTANCENEEDEDKEY or REFERRALTOKEY. The domain list is the standard set of SCORE circumstance domains used across the Data Exchange.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), section 6.2 reasons for seeking assistance and section 6.4 referrals to other services","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"The flag records a presenting need or the purpose of a referral, not anything delivered or achieved: a referral flag means a referral was made, not that the client took it up or got help. Reporting the reason is optional and, as the Protocols note, the real reason often only emerges after a client engages, so an unset flag is not evidence that a client had no training need.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_assistance_needed","madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_ref_referral_to"]},{"n":"UNIDENTIFIEDCLIENTATTENDANCE","d":"How many people attended a session without a client record being created for them.","full":"How many people attended a session without a client record being created for them. The Protocols define the item as \"the aggregate number of unidentified clients who attended a session\" and say it \"should be limited to large groups where the collection of client level information is not feasible\", which in practice means public events, information sessions and community outreach. These attendances are the only trace those people leave: they have no client row, no demographics and no person identifier, so nothing about them can be linked to the PLIDA spine.","dsrc":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), sections 2.6 and 5.2.2, and Table 9 priority requirements session level data","durl":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"The number of unidentified clients for the session","k":"count of unidentified attendees at a session","def":"A count of people on the session record, defaulting to zero, entered as a number up to 999, and constrained so that it cannot exceed the case-level figure carried in UNIDENTIFIEDCLIENTCASEMAX.","p":"2015 to 2024","s":"sourced","src":"DSS Data Exchange Protocols (Version 11, March 2024), sections 2.6 and 5.2.2, and Table 9 priority requirements session level data","url":"https://dex.dss.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/2024-03/1931-data-exchange-protocols_0.pdf","lim":"The number counts attendances at one session, not people: someone who comes to three sessions is counted three times, and the file gives no way to tell repeat attendance from new attendance. It also carries no age, sex, Indigenous status or cultural and linguistic background, so an event's audience cannot be described at all. Any person-level analysis of the Data Exchange silently drops these people while service-level counts keep them, which is the usual source of a mismatch between the two.","where":["madipge-dex-d-extended-15-current / special_session"]},{"n":"UNIDENTIFIEDCLIENTCASEMAX","d":"The case-level number of unidentified clients, carried onto the session row as the ceiling that session attendance sits under.","full":"The case-level number of unidentified clients, carried onto the session row as the ceiling that session attendance sits under. The Protocols explain the split: case-level numbers \"estimate the total number of unidentified clients who are anticipated to attend services\", the session-level number \"records how many unidentified clients actually attended that instance of service\", and this \"prevents double counting\". Their worked example is a case with two sessions of 100 unidentified clients each, which means up to 100 distinct people, not 200.
